## S5a conversation and planted-keyring closure (`3ca5dea`, `f60e9e9`, `905e5a3`, `fb55315`, `6b34512`)

**Explicit verdict for `3ca5dea`: APPROVED as the failing-first base,
cumulatively corrected by `f60e9e9` and `905e5a3`.** Its real-binary cases
drive the private-Xvfb UI with X input and clipboard selection, the production
helper and bundled Claude CLI through relay/netd to the fake TLS API. The
stream case therefore proves that a visible label grows before the held API
continues, not merely that a protocol row exists. BlackRobin's clean-export
red run on the prior implementation failed 17 of 26 e2e checks: there was no
growing bubble, no Stop row or interrupt behavior, and raw API/helper error
text appeared instead of the fixed sentences. The companion real-CLI error
suite failed its 401/429/529 cases and errored because the retry option did not
exist. The interrupt unit was already green and is correctly recorded as a
pin of existing SDK behavior, not claimed as an invented red.

**Explicit verdict for `f60e9e9`: APPROVED as the failing-first correction,
cumulatively completed by `905e5a3`.** It changes the contract from “two helper
errors make two bubbles” to one ending frame per prompt and adds the
second-ending-frame negative case. During green work its first fixture was
shown to be non-discriminating because an unconfirmed session is forgotten
after the first error; `905e5a3` fixes that setup by emitting
`session_opened` first. With that correction, removing the native no-busy
guard produces two “Agent error” bubbles and the test fails. This is valid
failing-first evidence for the intended production rule rather than a test
which passes because the validator discarded an unknown session.

**Explicit verdict for `905e5a3`: APPROVED.** The helper maps frame codes to
fixed user sentences and never renders a frame's message; a session error with
no running prompt is dropped as a second ending frame
(`src/agent_helper.c@905e5a3:244-301`). Stop is per-window, valid only for an
open busy session, emits one interrupt and suppresses that prompt's later
deltas/messages until its ending frame; a new prompt resets the stopping state
(`src/agent_helper.c@905e5a3:215-226,261-301,787-794`). The drawer owns one
stream label and buffer per window, finalizes exactly one message row, appends
“(stopped)” to the partial bubble, and returns focus to the input
(`src/agent_drawer.c@905e5a3:586-720,1126-1131`). All of this remains on the
GTK main context, and the stream buffer is allocated/destroyed with its drawer.

At the helper boundary, an SDK `AssistantMessage.error` discards its raw text
deltas and produces one error frame in place of the result; production keeps
the CLI's normal retry policy, while `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES=0` is added only
when hello carries the e2e test base URL
(`agent/host/zb_agent_host/chat.py@905e5a3:36-95,111-117`;
`agent/host/zb_agent_host/options.py@905e5a3:93-122`). The full-gate e2e passed
38/38 checks: streamed on-screen selection, stopped partial text, same-session
continuation, fixed 401/529 sentences, no raw server text, one error bubble,
and recovery when an interrupt ends with an error. The stop-state-reset and
second-ending-frame mutants both fail. The two new steps are dependencies of
the full `test` step, so they cannot be bypassed by the gate.

**Explicit verdict for `fb55315`: APPROVED as failing-first.** It plants an
API-key-shaped value through libsecret itself on a private D-Bus/keyring, then
uses the real binary and Send path. On `905e5a3`, two clean runs each failed
four of eight checks: the planted value started the helper and reached the fake
API. The regression requires no fake handoff seam: it checks the private
Secret Service precondition, no-token status and Secrets window, no connected
claim, no API request, no process copy, no row/log copy, and a fixed refusal
line (`tests/e2e/agent_secrets_test.py@fb55315:923-949`).

**Explicit verdict for `6b34512`: APPROVED.** Both Secret Service read paths
reuse the single Zig setup-token parser and additionally require its trimmed
slice to equal the complete stored value. The window lookup treats a malformed
item as absent, while the helper fetch returns `ZB_TOKEN_REFUSED` with only the
fixed `bad-shape` line. Neither branch duplicates the secret; libsecret's
original is released with `secret_password_free`, which wipes its allocation
(`src/agent_secrets.c@6b34512:107-116,201-224,319-344`). The no-fetch-check
mutant fails four assertions and the no-window-check mutant makes the connected
assertion fail. `planted-keyring` is registered in the full Secrets e2e; my
independent run passed the complete 222-check suite, including all eight
planted-item assertions. This closes the earlier planted-keyring S4 advisory.

I independently ran exact `6b34512` from a clean `git archive`, a fresh cache,
a 1,800-second bound and private Xvfb (seed `0xe1b462d8`): **Build Summary:
142/142 steps succeeded; 882/882 tests passed**. The top-level process exited
0. An intermediate “failed command” line was the output of an expected nested
negative-path test; its containing step passed. The EXIT trap deleted the

S5a adds visibly growing assistant bubbles, an active Stop state and fixed

## S5a real-screen acceptance at `6b34512` (2026-10-16)

**Status: USER-ACCEPTED on the real screen.** The orchestrator ran a clean
export of `6b34512` on the user's NVIDIA X11 screen with the throwaway S5a
home/profile, fake TLS API and media source disabled. The user confirmed all
three new visible states:

- one assistant bubble grew in place to “Streaming slowly into one bubble”;
- Stop finalized the partial bubble as “This will be stopped (stopped)” and
  restored the Ready state; and
- authentication and overload failures rendered only the fixed sentences
  “Claude rejected the saved token. Open Account to replace it.” and “Claude
  is busy; try again shortly.”

Neither the protocol rows nor stderr contained `SERVER TEXT` or `API Error`.
The supplied screenshots also showed selected bubble text, reconfirming the
previously accepted copyable-text behavior. This closes S5a's required
real-screen check; no visual S5a blocker remains.

**Observation pending owner confirmation, not presently a product blocker.**
During the first, deliberately out-of-order try, the user submitted `stream`,
`stop`, `again` and `token` while the first turn was still streaming. The
queued `stop` turn eventually rendered “This will be stopped but this never
shows” without a Stop click. The saved rows show FIFO was preserved: the first
turn reached Ready before `stop` became Busy, and `stop` reached Ready before
`again`, `token` and `busy` ran. Production likewise refuses to flush a queued
prompt while the window is busy (`src/agent_helper.c:201-227`).

The test server does not actually stall forever. Its documented and enforced
`STALL_MAX_S = 30.0` makes an unset event resume after 30 seconds
(`tests/e2e/fake_anthropic_api.py:10-15,35,64-83`), at which point it emits the
second delta and completes normally. That exactly explains the observed text;
a later queued request or SDK retry need not release the stream. I sent
BlackRobin the row trace in Agent Mail 5860. BlackRobin is running a focused
`queued-during-stall` case to confirm that no later API request starts before
the held response ends. Until that answer lands, the explanation is marked
**probable fixture timeout, pending BlackRobin confirmation**. If the focused
case instead shows a later request advancing the held turn, reopen this as a
product FIFO blocker and require the requested failing-first regression.

## S6a capture red and queued-stall guard (`375c79b`, `ce2aa62`, `aca7638`)

**Explicit verdict for `375c79b`: BLOCKED as landed, cumulatively APPROVED with
`aca7638`.**
The captured fixture itself is safe to commit. I scanned the exact Git object,
not a recollection of the real-screen run: it contains zero case-insensitive
`sk-ant` occurrences, zero setup-token shapes, zero JWT-, hex- or base64-like
32-character runs, and zero `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}` runs. Its pasted-code line is
exactly `<PASTED_CODE_MASKED>` and its token line is exactly `<TOKEN>`; no
asterisk run or visible tail from the user's pasted code remains. Client id,
challenge and state are placeholders, and the metadata contains no user path,
account or other credential. The committed fixture's SHA-256 is
`5cff86ab45fc5e2bbbe50153bfebae31ef90cf3dc2211690f813f351566e89e2`.

The fake is a faithful executable boundary for what this capture establishes:
it requires a pty, prints the captured lines and exact authorize parameter
order, generates fresh state/challenge values, logs synthetic received codes,
re-prompts for missing or foreign state, prints only a planted synthetic token,
and owns no socket. Its nine tests compare every output line with the fixture
and cover those boundary facts.

The blocking problem is in the red callback contract
(`tests/agent_auth_test.zig@375c79b:14-18,125-145,230-235`). It restricts the
opaque authorization code to URI-unreserved bytes and expressly rejects `+`.
The proposed D7b contract in Agent Mail 5858 instead permits visible non-space
ASCII, at most 512 bytes, with exactly one `#` delimiter. Because the captured
code is masked, it cannot prove that the provider will forever return only
`[A-Za-z0-9._~-]`; RFC 6749 Appendix A.11 likewise defines an authorization
code as opaque `1*VSCHAR`, not as an unreserved URI token. As written, the test
would force production to reject a terminal-safe code such as the unambiguous
query value `a%2Bb`. Fix the red forward so decoded visible punctuation is
accepted while SP, control bytes, DEL, `#`, malformed escapes and duplicated
parameters remain refused, or cite a provider guarantee and revise D7b before
the green. I mailed this BLOCKER to BlueBeaver as Agent Mail 5865. The red's
stale “rev 16.17” label is also to be corrected to rev 16.18 in its follow-up;
`ce2aa62` legitimately took 16.17.

(`+` becomes SP and `%XX` becomes its byte), accepts decoded ASCII `0x21-0x7e`
except `#`, and has concrete passing cases for `%2B`, `%2F`, `%3D` and the
remaining visible punctuation. It retains negative cases for SP, CR, LF, ESC,
DEL, NUL, non-ASCII bytes, malformed escapes, `#`, empty and duplicated code;
the separate oracle and 10,000-pair generator use the same public contract.
The earlier unreserved-only green draft fails two of ten tests, so the
correction is red against the implementation it is meant to prevent. The
fixture-secret regression now uses the same 32-character threshold as the
independent review census. This closes Agent Mail 5865 and the associated
SHOULD-for-test in 5863.

**Explicit verdict for `ce2aa62`: APPROVED.** The real-helper half holds an API
response after its first delta, shows the queued user bubble, and proves for a

### S6a part 2 (`edd2c6c`)

**Explicit verdict for `edd2c6c`: BLOCKED.** The native frame validator is
bounded, exact and noncommitting on rejection, and the helper correctly uses a
wide pty, a fixed environment, process-group cleanup, fd-4-only token delivery
and a one-shot lifetime. The 151/151, 900/900 clean gate and the reported eight
protocol plus twelve helper killed mutants are good evidence for those covered
paths. Three production contracts remain uncovered and broken:

1. **BLOCKER — the authorize URL is not exact.**
   `agent/host/zb_agent_host/login.py:69-82` accepts the right parameter names,
   redirect URI, nonempty state and `response_type=code`, but it accepts changed
   or empty `code`, `scope`, `code_challenge_method`, `client_id` and
   `code_challenge`. The captured contract fixes `code=true`,
   `scope=user:inference` and `code_challenge_method=S256`
   (`plan:610-615`). A lookalike URL can therefore be forwarded as the CLI's
   authorize URL. Add near-miss table cases, require those fixed values and
   require nonempty client/challenge values (or explicitly pin the captured
   client id if that is the intended contract).
2. **BLOCKER — a later code overwrites the first pending code.**
   `login.py:222-227` assigns `self.code` unconditionally. If callback capture
   and a manual paste both arrive before the next CLI prompt, the second value
   replaces the first, contrary to D7b's “the first one to arrive is used”
   (`plan:430-432`). A slow-prompt regression must send two valid codes before
   `need_code` and prove only the first reaches the CLI.
3. **BLOCKER — terminal completion and token delivery race cancellation.**
   `login.py:189-206` performs an unsynchronized check-then-set in `end()`, so
   the PTY and frame threads can both emit terminal frames. `hand_off()` also
   writes and closes fd 4 before trying to claim `done`; a concurrent cancel
   can win `ended` while the PTY thread still delivers the token. Use a terminal
   claim separate from the screen lock and add deterministic interleaving tests
   proving one terminal frame and no fd-4 token when cancellation wins.

These findings were mailed to BlueBeaver as Agent Mail 5967. The green gate did
not exercise the missing interleavings, so it does not close them.

### PagePort timeout regression (`f73305e`)

**Explicit verdict for `f73305e`: APPROVED.** This is a test-only correction.
The old script created a pending promise with no reachable promise or resolver;
WebKit may collect it and end the call with “Completion handler for function
call is no longer reachable,” which production correctly maps to `EvalFailed`
rather than `Timeout`. The new script retains the resolver on the page global,
matching the existing `__zbHold1` pattern, while preserving the 100 ms timeout
and the same production PagePort chain (`src/webkit.zig:785-792`).

The root cause is demonstrated, not merely made less likely: BlackRobin's
standalone old form ended early in 31–42 ms in 3/3 runs while the held form
remained pending for 8 s in 3/3; the loaded live test failed with the exact old
message in 3/3 runs and passed 152/152 in 3/3 with the held resolver; the unit
binary also passed 152/152 three times. No production code changed. A separate
full gate was correctly deferred because BlueBeaver held the exclusive slot.

## S6b1 split and paste-path red (`2713c20`, `f18a5f1`)

### Plan rev 16.18.3

The architectural split is sound. S6b1 can prove the Secrets-window → native
login owner → dedicated login netd → sandboxed one-shot helper → fd 4 → S4
store chain without pretending that the auth WebView already exists. The plan
also keeps chat's network capability unchanged, gives the login netd its own
directory and lifetime, and leaves the callback/isolation surface wholly in
S6b2 (`plan:2053-2073`). Moving that ownership into the new
`agent_login.c` avoids coupling login lifetime to the long-lived chat helper.

**Explicit verdict for `2713c20`: BLOCKED (one slice-gate contract is still
missing).** The global UI rule says every UI slice adds and names its own
real-hardware case and cannot be approved before the user's screen passes it
(`plan:1209-1235,1393`). S6b1 adds four Secrets-window controls and seven
sentences, and its security boundary explicitly depends on discovering whether
the real `claude setup-token` needs another writable config path
(`plan:2054-2064`). Nevertheless the split assigns “the real-screen check”
only to S6b2 (`plan:2073`), and the login-network census still says merely
“during S6b's” check (`plan:639`). Rev 16.18.4 must give **S6b1 its own named
real-screen case**: exercise the paste UI and fixed sentences with the real
setup-token flow, record the CONNECT census, and prove the current read-only
mounts suffice (or revise them before S6b1 approval). S6b2 then keeps its
separate auth-window/callback/isolation real-screen case. This prevents the
new UI and the allowlist exception from landing one slice before their required
hardware and real-CLI qualification.

### Failing-first e2e

The committed red is genuinely red at the outer production trigger: it opens
the drawer and Secrets window with X input, clicks the planned Sign-in control,
and observes the store/fake/lifetime boundaries rather than calling native
login functions directly. The fake's scratchpad relocation is coherent with
the sandbox, contains only a synthetic setup-token-shaped canary, and its
narrow test passes **10/10**. `py_compile` also passes for all five changed
Python files. BlueBeaver supplied repeatable clean-export red evidence: three
runs, each 15 checks with the same seven intended failures.

**Explicit verdict for `f18a5f1`: BLOCKED-for-tests.** Its direction and red
evidence are accepted, but a correct green cannot satisfy the committed test
as written and several claims are not actually proved:

1. **BLOCKER-for-tests — process census false-positive.** `procs()` matches a
   needle anywhere in every argv, so `login_netds()` counts bwrap/launcher and

   `during-sign-in` assertion requires exactly one (`:255-265`). Restrict the

3. **BLOCKER-for-tests — “paste path” never pastes and never rejects malformed
   input.** `SignIn.paste` synthesizes one key at a time (`:83-92,146-150`),

   private-Xvfb `Clipboard` plus Ctrl+V for this synthetic, non-secret code, and
   add a malformed value (no `#`, extra `#`, internal whitespace, or invalid
   byte) that shows “That doesn't look like a sign-in code.”, sends no code to
   the fake, and stores nothing. Otherwise a product that breaks Ctrl+V or
   forwards grammar-invalid input passes S6.4.
4. **BLOCKER-for-tests — close does not prove its stated teardown.** The file
   header and commit message say closing the Secrets window leaves no login
   helper, netd or directory, but `case_close` checks only the cancelled row,

## S5c design, S6b1 qualification, and MS1 exact-shape follow-ups (`5ad5c88`, `2e725c7`, `91b6f81`, `58551bb`, `50bc1bd`)

### S5c plan rev 16.20 and 16.20.1

The private-Xvfb probe results in rev 16.20 are useful and the two user
decisions are accepted: long unbroken runs should gain display-only break
opportunities, and the near-term credential fix is transcript cleanup while
the token stand-in becomes the named deferred `SX-standin` slice. The plan is
not yet implementation-ready, however.

**Explicit verdict for `5ad5c88`: BLOCKED.** The appended S5.6 contract
contradicts the still-active acceptance test immediately above it:

1. `plan:2022-2027` combines 50,000 deltas and a 2 MiB final under a 64 MiB
   RSS bound and requires a `DRAWER idles` row, while `plan:2037-2039` removes
   that row, limits the 64 MiB claim to the small-text flood, and permits 200
   MiB for a maximum reply. Replace the old case with separate authoritative
   flood and maximum-reply cases instead of leaving both contracts active.
2. `plan:2035` says every reply is whole with “no size cut”, while
   `plan:2039-2041` retains the helper's 256 KiB cap. The intended decision is
   no *new* 32 KiB cut below the existing cap; state that precisely.
3. Exact-copy coverage must include whole and partial selections crossing an
   inserted U+200B, multibyte UTF-8, and source text that already contains
   U+200B. Define what counts as a character/whitespace/run, so cleanup cannot
   strip a user's original zero-width space.
4. The single pending idle needs an explicit destruction contract and red:
   cancel/remove it when a drawer, window or session dies, and prove no late
   UI update or use-after-free.
5. S5c-1 visibly changes wrapping, copying and fold responsiveness but names
   no section 7.1 real-screen check. Add a case for the user's real display;
   private-Xvfb timing remains the automated gate.

**Explicit verdict for `2e725c7`: BLOCKED.** “Cleanup now, stand-in later” is
an accepted scope decision, but the transcript scrub has no safe persistence
or failure protocol yet:

1. The scrub must finish successfully before the helper emits the terminal
   result/error and before any queued next prompt begins. Open/read/write/fsync
   failure must fail closed with a fixed sentence and stop/refuse that session.
2. The plan must choose a mutation compatible with a persistent CLI process.
   A variable-length rewrite or atomic replacement can leave a CLI that still
   owns the old file descriptor appending to an unlinked inode. Use a proven
   close/reopen boundary, or a bounded equal-length in-place overwrite plus
   fsync, and test that later turns preserve a valid transcript.
3. A crash after the server echo reaches disk but before the reply ends leaves
   the token indefinitely. Add startup/pre-session recovery that cleans this
   residue before a new session, with a kill-at-that-cut test, or obtain an
   explicit user acceptance of that residual risk.
4. Replace stale `plan:2044-2048`: the helper stderr ring no longer exists and
   an app-side redactor cannot independently expose the canary because raw API
   text never reaches the app. Specify exactly which saved fields/patterns are
   scrubbed. The automation-token transcript canary is not a known helper
   value unless the helper actually receives it, so either define a general
   server-error scrub or remove that assertion.

## S5c plan rev 16.20.2 (`1f0c04e`)

Rev 16.20.2 is a substantial correction. It replaces, rather than appends to,
the stale S5.6/S5.7 text. The S5.6 design now has one coherent contract: the
64 MiB bound applies only to the 50,000-delta case, the larger bubble has its

### Transcript scrub rev 16.20.3

The whole-life 0.25 s monitor closes the original indefinite post-result
window. The revision also removes the undeclared pause seam, makes the four
lifecycle outcomes explicit, enumerates file-operation fault injection and
resets on an observed inode replacement or shrink. It does not yet make the
crash/cursor story fail closed.

**Explicit verdict for `5baf1bc`: BLOCKED.**

   newline-terminated records are scanned (`plan:2124`), including at helper

   until a later newline (`:2155`). A killed writer can leave a final partial
   JSONL line containing a complete token; no newline may ever arrive, so the
   next helper can emit `ready` while the credential remains forever. Scan
   complete matches in the partial suffix while retaining the cursor at that
   line's start, and add idle/start crash-residue reds with no final newline.

   skipped. The red at `:2156` must perform that exact sequence without an
   intermediate scan. Identity and size must also come from `fstat` on the
   same opened regular, no-follow fd that is read/written; a path `stat`
   followed by `open` otherwise reintroduces a replacement TOCTOU. Define a

   plan states exit 3 and no `session_ended` for both paths

   fault, each asserting exit 3, no `session_ended`, and no later frame. Direct

## Transcript scrub plan rev 16.20.4 (`def9c2a`)

Rev 16.20.4 materially improves the scrub contract. It replaces the unsafe
cursor with a whole-file rescan keyed by fd-derived metadata, scans the partial
tail, names the quiet and polling bounds, rejects a symlink/non-regular final
component, and adds helper-level monitor, `end_session`, `shutdown`, prompt-end
and startup failure reds (`plan:2128-2198`). Those changes close the original
partial-tail, leaf-fd TOCTOU and lifecycle-supervision findings in the ordinary
case. Three boundary problems remain.

**Explicit verdict for `def9c2a`: BLOCKED.**

1. **BLOCKER — leaf-only `O_NOFOLLOW` does not confine the scan beneath the
   transcript root.** `plan:2128-2131` still opens a full pathname found below
   `state/projects/*`. `O_NOFOLLOW` rejects only a symlink in the final
   component; a symlinked `projects` or workspace directory is followed, and
   the final JSONL then passes `fstat` as an ordinary file outside the agent
   transcript tree. A local probe reproduced exactly that success. Pin the
   projects directory fd and walk every component with no-follow directory
   opens, or use an equivalent beneath/no-symlink resolution primitive. Add
   an intermediate-directory symlink red and require the outside canary to
   remain byte-identical.
2. **BLOCKER — the whole-file polling work is unbounded.** The cost statement
   says a transcript is “a few MB at most” (`plan:2139-2142`), but no contract
   caps the persistent JSONL files; S5b deliberately retains them and one
   assistant reply alone may be 256 KiB. A changing 100 MiB file at the named
   0.25 s poll interval implies roughly 400 MiB/s of rereads. Define and
   enforce a transcript/scan-work bound and its user-visible failure, or use a
   bounded incremental design with a fail-closed prefix-integrity check. The
   reds need a large, continuously appended transcript and a liveness/CPU/RSS
   bound.
3. **BLOCKER — an unqualified star-run extension corrupts ordinary content.**
   The plan masks token characters following any run of `*` (`plan:2137`). A
   legitimate transcript containing `********documentation` is therefore
   changed, contradicting the same-length/every-other-byte invariant in the
   red suite (`plan:2180`). Track only scrubber-created pending ranges, with
   restart behavior defined, or use another provenance rule that cannot
   collide with user/model text. Add complete-line and EOF negatives for
   ordinary star runs followed by `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

**BLOCKER-for-tests:** the truncate/regrow red grows past the prior size
(`plan:2185`), so `st_size` alone catches it and the new `st_mtime_ns` member is
not pinned. Regrow to exactly the old size with a token before the old offset.
Also state explicitly that a pending unterminated match is revisited when its
quiet deadline expires even though the ordinary monitor scans only when the
change key moves (`plan:2145-2152`).

The deferred SX-standin notes are not treated as an approved implementation
contract; the plan correctly keeps that slice subject to a later user
decision. `git diff --check def9c2a^ def9c2a` passed. No browser or full gate
was run for this docs-only review. Findings were mailed as Agent Mail 6019.
The approved linear push-through SHA remains **`da3028f`**.

## Transcript scrub plan rev 16.20.5 (`5be4c4c`)

Rev 16.20.5 closes the four narrow findings from the rev-16.20.4 review:
the walk now uses one-component `openat` calls with `O_NOFOLLOW`, the plan
replaces the unsupported “few MB” assumption with an explicit monitor rate,
mask extension is limited to scrubber-created ranges, and the reds now pin an
exact-size truncate/regrow plus the quiet-deadline revisit
(`plan:2128-2235`). Those corrections are real, but the replacement design
introduces five new boundary failures.

**Explicit verdict for `5be4c4c`: BLOCKED.**

1. **BLOCKER — the whole-life `projects` fd can become detached from the live
   writable bind.** The plan pins `state/projects` once and keeps that fd for
   the helper's lifetime (`plan:2129-2136`). D12 makes that directory writable.
   A writer can rename it and put a replacement at the live path; the CLI then
   writes into the replacement while the scrubber scans only the unlinked old
   tree. Reopen and identity-check the current component from a pinned parent
   on every census, or provide an equivalent fail-closed replacement check.
   Add a post-`ready` directory-swap red that writes a token into the current
   replacement and permits no ending/ready frame while it remains.
2. **BLOCKER — directly mapping a mutable transcript cannot implement the
   promised controlled failure.** A concurrent truncate below a mapped page
   makes a later access raise SIGBUS, not an injectable `mmap` error that the
   helper can convert to exit 3 (`plan:2140-2144,2182-2194`). A local child
   probe mapped 8 MiB read-only, truncated its fd to zero, touched the former
   last byte, and exited **135/SIGBUS**. Use a race-safe streaming matcher or a
   stable snapshot, and add a real-helper truncate-during-scan red.
3. **BLOCKER — the token bucket and worker ownership are not executable
   contracts.** Capacity, initial fill and fairness are unspecified
   (`plan:2166-2172`). A 64 MiB-capacity bucket can never admit the specified
   100 MiB whole-file scan; an accumulating bucket merely delays and then
   bursts one monolithic scan. A Python thread alone also does not establish
   responsiveness while Python matching owns the GIL, and the plan does not
   serialize monitor and lifecycle scans that mutate shared change keys,
   pending ranges and provenance. Define bounded work quanta, cross-chunk
   state, capacity/fill/fairness, and one owner for every scan/mutation.
4. **BLOCKER — mask provenance becomes stale on same-inode rewrite.** A range
   recorded by `(st_dev, st_ino)` survives the plan's own truncate/regrow case
   (`plan:2150-2158`). If replacement content puts legitimate
   `********documentation` at that old range, the stale record authorizes
   corrupting `documentation`. Invalidate or revalidate provenance on every
   non-append change and add that same-inode false-positive red.
5. **BLOCKER-for-tests — the process counters do not measure mmap work.** On
   this host, touching a fresh 32 MiB mapping moved `/proc/self/io:rchar` by
   only 101 bytes, so the helper oracle at `plan:2232-2235` can pass while an
   arbitrary mapping is scanned. Touching a 100 MiB mapping raised `VmRSS`
   from about 12.8 MiB to 115.3 MiB, contradicting the promised <32 MiB growth
   unless pages are actively discarded/chunked. Count logical scan bytes at
   the scrubber seam and bound resident work by construction; retain the
   process-level frame-liveness test separately.

`git diff --check 5be4c4c^ 5be4c4c` passed. No browser/full gate was run for
this docs-only review. The findings and local probes were sent to BlackRobin
as Agent Mail 6023.

### Transcript scrub plan rev 16.20.6 (`a69b459`)

Rev 16.20.6 materially closes the five design failures in Agent Mail 6023:
each census re-walks from the pinned root rather than retaining a stale
`projects` fd; `pread` replaces SIGBUS-prone `mmap`; one thread owns scans and
state; bounded chunks and internal logical-byte accounting replace the
underspecified token bucket and invalid `/proc` oracle; and mask provenance is
gone. Replacement, chunk-edge, truncation, memory and lifecycle tests are now
named. Three contradictions/races remain before that design is executable.

**Explicit verdict for `a69b459`: BLOCKED.**

1. **BLOCKER — the matcher masks and defers the same bytes.** The carried
   matcher says every token byte is masked as it is read through EOF
   (`plan:2158-2161`), while the timing contract says a monitor leaves an
   unterminated generic match at EOF untouched (`plan:2174-2180`). Define an
   offset/length candidate that defers `pwrite` until a terminator, or until a
   lifecycle scan accepts EOF. This remains memory-bounded because it retains
   offsets and automaton state rather than the match bytes. The monitor-EOF
   negative must assert byte identity before a lifecycle scan masks it.
2. **BLOCKER — a re-walk is not a stable lifecycle census.** A `projects` or
   workspace replacement, a new directory entry, or a short read can occur
   after that component was listed/opened but before the lifecycle request
   returns. The current text treats a short read as success and can therefore
   release an ending frame while the new live tree contains a token
   (`plan:2138-2157,2182-2203`). Before a lifecycle scan succeeds, revalidate
   the directory generation/entry set and each file's post-scan key; if any
   moved, changed or read short, rescan with a bounded fail-closed outcome.
   Add a mid-lifecycle directory/file swap red that permits no ending frame
   until the replacement is clean.
3. **BLOCKER — the change key omits the non-restorable metadata clock.** The
   current `(dev, ino, size, mtime_ns)` key (`plan:2150-2152`) can be restored
   after a same-inode, same-size rewrite with `utime`; `state/projects` is a
   writable sandbox state directory. Include `ctime_ns`, which an unprivileged
   writer cannot restore, and add a red that restores the old mtime after the
   rewrite but is still rescanned.

The findings were sent to BlackRobin as Agent Mail 6033.

## Transcript scrub plan rev 16.20.7 (`87c9ea1`)

Rev 16.20.7 closes the three mechanisms reported against `a69b459`:

- an open generic match is now an offset/length candidate, not bytes written
  speculatively, so a terminated match can be masked while a monitor leaves an
  EOF candidate untouched (`plan:2158-2162`);
- a lifecycle scan re-walks and revalidates the directory generations,
  listings and post-scan file keys, retries a changed or short-read pass, and
  fails closed after the named three-pass bound (`plan:2183-2187,2198-2217`);
  and
- `st_ctime_ns` joins the change key, with a same-size rewrite that restores
  mtime as its red (`plan:2150-2152,2227-2232`).

The new reds correctly cover monitor-versus-lifecycle EOF behavior, tree and
file replacement during revalidation, repeated instability, a lifecycle short
read, and restored mtime. One state transition remains missing.

**Explicit verdict for `87c9ea1`: BLOCKED.**

- **BLOCKER — dropping an EOF candidate can make the lifecycle scan skip it.**
  A monitor that reaches an unterminated generic candidate drops it and writes
  nothing (`plan:2161`). If that successful monitor commits the file's current
  change key, the later lifecycle scan sees an unchanged file and skips it
  under the “scan when changed” rule and stated lifecycle cost
  (`plan:2150-2152,2167`). It then cannot perform the promised lifecycle mask
  at `plan:2178-2180`. Specify either that such a monitor scan does not commit
  the clean key, or retain a per-file `pending_eof` flag keyed to file identity
  that forces lifecycle rescan even when metadata is unchanged. Define how the
  state is cleared or invalidated after masking, identity replacement or
  content change. The existing several-polls-then-`end_session` red is the
  correct test and need not change.

The implementation has several strong properties. The real-binary e2e drives

1. **BLOCKER — a UTF-8 character that does not fit at one timed flush is

   `agent/host/zb_agent_host/chat.py:128-143` tracks only the byte count. When
   `utf8_prefix(piece, room)` is empty, it breaks that flush and then clears
   `pending`, but does not make forwarding terminal. A later flush can put a
   later one-byte character into the remaining byte. Driving the production
   `Session.prompt` with timed stream events
   `['a' * (MESSAGE_TEXT_MAX - 1), '界', 'x']` produced 262,144 bytes ending
   in `aaax`; the required longest prefix is 262,143 bytes ending in `aaaa`,
   and the source does not start with the emitted result. The existing over-cap
   test's chunk/timing pattern misses this cross-flush boundary. Once no code
   point fits, delta forwarding must stay ended for the reply; add the exact
   timed-flush regression and a deletion/condition mutant.
2. **BLOCKER — that same boundary can disable overflow termination.** The
   native timer starts only after received deltas total at least 262,144 bytes
   (`src/agent_helper.c:295-301`). A correct longest prefix may stop at 262,141,
   262,142 or 262,143 bytes when the next code point does not fit. An endless
   multibyte source can therefore cross the logical cap while the app never
   arms its timer and never reports `Agent output overflow`. The regression
   must drive this boundary through the native app: no later source text fills
   the remainder, the running turn is interrupted after the bound, and the
   next prompt succeeds. The cap-crossing signal/count must not depend on
   violating the exact-prefix rule.

plan is absent.** Rev 16.20.10 requires `tests/manual/real_screen_check.py`

### `4f41929` — BLOCKED-for-tests

The committed file is a useful failing-first test, but it is not yet the

Two test-hygiene defects must be fixed before this runner is registered:

1. **BLOCKER-for-tests — a timeout can orphan the browser tree.** `run_case`
   uses `subprocess.run(..., timeout=600)` (`:41-45`). Python kills only that
   wrapper on timeout. The intended manual implementation starts zigBrowser
   in a new session, so the browser, netd, helper, X clients, and fixture
   processes can survive after the wrapper is killed—the same orphan class
   this repository has already had to fix. The automatic test must own a
   process group and terminate/reap the entire tree on timeout, or use the
   existing lifecycle launcher with that guarantee.
2. **BLOCKER-for-tests — every automatic run leaks its output directory.** The
   default path and the nonempty-path case use `mkdtemp()` (`:42,65`) without a
   cleanup. A successful run deliberately writes rows, stderr, and captures.

## Voice and Windows plan review (`9663333`)

Commit `9663333` adds three TDD plans and their three research documents. The
research supports the principal platform choices, and the plans correctly
record the user's decisions: Pocket TTS is the bundled primary voice,
read-aloud defaults on, cloning requires explicit consent and stays local,
whisper medium is bundled in every installer, and macOS and Windows are the
primary targets. `git diff --check 9663333^ 9663333` passes. No runtime gate
was appropriate for this docs-only review.

The plans are not yet safe to implement concurrently. Their shared subsystem
contracts disagree, and each plan has additional dependency or test gaps.

### Voice-output / TTS plan rev 2.2 — BLOCKED

1. **BLOCKER — the alleged shared audio/model/settings/window contract is not
   shared.** The TTS plan says the pieces are “named the same” and first owner
   wins (`TTS:258-275`), but it assigns them to `src/audio.zig`, `src/audio.c`,
   `src/models.zig`, `src/voice_settings.zig`, and `src/voice_window.c`
   (`TTS:313-319,1075-1081,1107-1109,1242-1243`). The STT plan instead names
   `src/voice/audio.zig`, `src/voice/audio_miniaudio.c`,
   `src/voice/models.zig`, `src/voice/voice_config.zig`, and
   `src/voice_settings_window.c` (`STT:162-175,338-346`). It also specifies
   `AudioSource`/`AudioSink` vtables and one miniaudio context, which the TTS
   files do not adopt. None of these prospective files exists at HEAD, so
   “whichever lands first” would let the first implementation silently choose
   an incompatible ABI and force the other plan into shared-file rewrites.
   Create one named shared foundation slice with one path set, API, owner,
   red suite, and dependency edge from both plans.
2. **BLOCKER — `voice.json` has no single-writer or lost-update contract.** TTS
   promises to validate only `read_aloud` and preserve `dictation` bytes
   unchanged (`TTS:267,273-275,318`), while STT promises one parsed/versioned
   schema (`STT:319-325`). Atomic replacement alone does not prevent two open
   native windows from reading the same generation and replacing each other's
   changes. The shared foundation must own serialization and either serialize
   mutations or use a generation/compare-and-retry protocol. Reds must hold
   both windows open, interleave writes to the two sections, and prove both
   changes and unknown raw fields survive.
3. **BLOCKER — verified model bytes are not pinned through consumption.** V3.1
   verifies names, sizes, and hashes and then the speech engine opens the model
   by path (`TTS:1096-1127`). The plan has no handle/buffer identity rule or red
   for replacing a verified file before ONNX Runtime consumes it. Load from
   the verified bytes or a pinned file handle/platform identity, and mutate or
   replace the path at the verify/use seam in a failing-first test.
4. **BLOCKER — the macOS cloning UI is ordered before the UI it needs.** The
   global order places C1-C3 before M2 (`TTS:858-865`); C1's only UI file is
   GTK `src/voice_window.c` (`TTS:1272-1298`), C2 gives the Macs only a
   self-test WAV path (`TTS:1308-1311`), and C3 names no AppKit implementation.
   The AppKit Voice window does not exist until M2
   (`TTS:1324-1339`). Split the platform legs or make the Mac enrollment,
   delete, and real-screen checks depend on M2 with named AppKit files/tests.
   The same dependency omission affects the S4 Personal Voice UI: it is
   declared after S2 only (`TTS:1454-1463,1550`) although its control must live
   in M2's AppKit Voice window.
5. **BLOCKER — the shipping/package slice has no component dependencies.**
   V3.5 asserts that Linux, macOS, and Windows packages contain `zb-speech`,
   ONNX Runtime, models, licenses, and UI credits (`TTS:1142-1166`), yet its
   dependency row names only legal decision OD7 (`TTS:1541`). It must depend
   on V3 plus the relevant macOS/Windows runtime and packaging milestones
   (including the component-producing M1/W1 and platform installer gates), or
   be explicitly split into per-platform packaging legs.

The license/download-gate terms and Pocket TTS runtime route remain explicit
decision gates rather than hidden assumptions; those open decisions are not
additional review defects.

### Voice-input / STT plan rev 2 — BLOCKED

1. **BLOCKER — the same shared-layer and `voice.json` ownership conflicts
   above apply here.** STT explicitly proposes that whichever plan lands first
   owns the audio layer and that the sections register into one Voice window
   (`STT:336-346`), but its paths and ABI differ from TTS. A single shared
   slice must replace both competing definitions before VS1, VS3, VS6, V2, V3,
   or V5 begins.
2. **BLOCKER — the model integrity claim has a verify/use race.** The plan
   hashes the file “before `whisper_init_from_file`” and optionally caches that
   result by `(size, mtime, inode)` (`STT:248-252`), then the closure passes the
   path to `whisper_init_from_file` (`STT:490-494`). Reopening a mutable path
   does not prove the bytes loaded are the bytes hashed; the proposed cache
   makes that guarantee weaker. Use `whisper_init_from_buffer` over verified
   bytes, or a pinned handle and an explicitly proven platform mapping, and
   add replacement/mutation races at the seam. “The bundle is read-only” is
   an install policy, not an identity proof on the per-user Windows layout or
   a test override.
3. **BLOCKER-for-tests — VS0.2 is allowed to have no red.** Its instruction is
   to record a failing cross-target compile “or record that it compiled first
   time” (`STT:543-548`). That violates the repository's red-first contract.
   Add a missing registration/object oracle or a small build mutant so this
   slice necessarily demonstrates a red before it joins `cross-check`.
4. **BLOCKER-for-tests — the no-audio-on-disk oracle is neither hermetic nor
   complete.** VS4.3 scans global `/tmp` for files newer than the test start
   that happen to look like RIFF or 64 KiB of f32 data (`STT:693-697`). On a
   shared host this can fail on another process and can pass audio written in
   a different encoding or directory. Run the process inside a test-owned
   mount/temp namespace with an auditable writable-file boundary, or add a
   production file-open/write census, then assert no audio-derived write over
   complete/cancel/error paths. Keep the buffer-zeroization accessor as the
   independent memory oracle.

The chosen medium variant remains an explicit O1 decision before packaging;
the plan correctly does not disguise that as settled.

### Windows launch plan rev 2 — BLOCKED

1. **BLOCKER — WS8.7 is omitted from its own hard gate.** The no-network
   `zb-speech` confinement class, its negative network probes, and its mutant
   are specified at `Windows:1411-1436`, but the milestone gate runs only
   WS8.1-WS8.6 (`Windows:1466`). W1 treats WS8.7 as a hard prerequisite, so a

3. **BLOCKER — uninstall is allowed to report completion while privileged

**SHOULD:** the research/line audit is intentionally pinned to `032a2c9`, but
WS0 implementation has since landed in stages. Before WS1 work uses this as

approved WS0 Linux foundation from the still-required two-host Windows

Because all three plan artifacts are blocked, `9663333` is not an approved

## Windows resolver live-host fix (`6e0a1b1`)

### `6e0a1b1` — BLOCKED-for-tests (production fix is sound)

The code change is correct. PowerShell binds the P/Invoke's access parameter as
`uint`; the old literal `0x80000000` is parsed as a negative signed value before
that call, so the cast can fail before `CreateFile` reaches Windows. Passing
`dwDesiredAccess = 0` is the documented metadata-query form and is sufficient
for `GetFinalPathNameByHandle`; changing the share mask to read+write avoids an
unnecessary write-sharing denial. Keeping only
`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`, without `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`, is also
the correct direction: the handle follows a junction instead of returning the
junction object's in-root name. SSH/PowerShell/CreateFile failures propagate
nonzero and `gate.sh:88-101` converts them to `DENY`, so the observed error 448
is fail-closed.

The reported live red/green is credible and directly explains why the prior
fake-SSH suite missed the defect: before the change every real path failed at
the P/Invoke conversion; after it an ordinary in-root path and `C:\Windows`
resolve. The existing hermetic suite remains green (**15/15** in 3.424 s),
`bash -n` and `git diff --check` pass.

One TDD gap prevents approval of the commit as the durable WS0 fix:

- **BLOCKER-for-tests — no committed test executes the real PowerShell/PInvoke
  body.** `6e0a1b1` changes only `resolve_path.sh`. The Linux tests observe its
  generated command and fake the SSH result; the commit message explicitly
  confirms that this let the old all-path failure survive. A future reversion
  to `0x80000000` therefore leaves all 15 registered tests green. Add a Windows
  gate case that invokes the production resolver on an existing in-root path
  and requires the exact resolved result, then invokes it on an escaping
  junction (or the present build's documented unresolvable junction) and
  requires `DENY`. Record the old revision red and this one green. A positive
  in-root junction case may remain a tracked availability refinement, but the
  ordinary real `CreateFile` path cannot remain live evidence only.

This verdict does not reject the safer production change and does not ask for
it to be reverted. It requires a fix-forward regression before cumulative WS0
approval. The approved linear push-through boundary remains the already-pushed
**`da3028f`**.

## Plan rev 16.20.13: completed capped bubbles and prompt correlation (`e1d44c5`)

### `e1d44c5` — BLOCKED (plan/tests)

The revision correctly closes the user-visible defect from `5aea621`: a
completed capped bubble is immutable, a later shorter `assistant_message`
cannot replace it, and a `result` or `error` finalizes a delta-only stream
without discarding its text (`plan:2182-2184`). The proposed
`capped-finite` case observes the completed bubble through Ctrl+A/C after the
shorter message and result, so it exercises the exact production failure
(`plan:2203`). The helper-side escaped-text case also distinguishes a text
payload below the content cap from its larger JSON representation
(`plan:2184,2201,2205`).

The prompt-correlation contract is still incomplete:

- **BLOCKER — `prompt_id` identifies only the cap, not the prompt-scoped
  stream.** D7 adds the id to `prompt` and `reply_capped`, while
  `assistant_delta`, `assistant_message`, `result`, and session-scoped
  `error` remain session-only (`plan:406,418-423`). A delayed old delta can
  append to a new bubble, an old message can replace/end it, and an old result
  or error can end the new prompt and release another queued prompt. This is
  the real production shape today: the parsed frames are session-only
  (`src/agent_protocol.zig:20-24,152-185`), the C frames have no prompt id
  (`src/agent_frames.zig:27-38,73-94`), and dispatch selects only by session
  and busy state (`src/agent_helper.c:285-345`). If `prompt_id` is the
  correlation mechanism, every prompt-scoped delta, message, cap, result, and
  session error needs it; helper-wide null errors remain explicitly
  uncorrelated. The plan must define active-id clearing, exactly-once ending,
  and session-close behavior, with stale/missing/future/duplicate ending-frame
  reds across prompt transitions. As written, the claim that the id covers
  every late frame (`plan:2190`) is false.
- **BLOCKER — identity does not replace within-prompt ordering.** A legitimate
  cap means the helper already emitted the reply's maximal delta prefix. The
  revision instead drops `delta-seen` (`plan:2190`) and has no red for a cap
  carrying the current prompt id before that prompt's first delta
  (`plan:2193-2198`). Such a malformed frame can arm the overflow timer and
  put a truncation marker on an empty/current bubble. Keep a per-prompt
  `delta_seen` state in addition to the id, reject current-id/no-delta without
  committing state, and keep the old ordering red.
- **BLOCKER-for-tests — the drawer's local byte-cap path has no no-shrink
  red.** The app contract covers both an explicit `reply_capped` and a stream
  capped by the drawer's own byte limit (`plan:2183`), but `capped-finite`
  covers only the explicit-frame path. A native scripted-helper case must
  exceed the app cap with deltas, send no cap frame, then send a shorter
  `assistant_message` and `result`; clipboard text must remain exactly the
  prefix plus one marker.
- **SHOULD — make the canonical table internally consistent and bound the
  id.** The `reply_capped` row says rev 16.20.13 replaces the old ordering
  rule, but retains that rule verbatim (`plan:420`), while the new section says
  it is dropped. Rewrite the row as one normative rule. State the positive
  integer bound/overflow behavior and per-session reset for `prompt_id` too.

## Orchestrator decision: S5d prompt-correlation split

The orchestrator's post-`ec92508` decision resolves the scope question from
`2b5f074`: full prompt-frame correlation is now the named slice **S5d,
“prompt correlation,”** owned by BlackRobin and scheduled immediately after
S5c. It is a hard prerequisite of S6c onward and of any later slice that runs
more than one prompt in a session under Stop or interrupt. S5c deliberately
keeps only `reply_capped`'s `prompt_id` and the per-prompt streamed/capped
state.

This is an acceptable architectural split. Therefore `6d812b4` item 1 is
**DEFERRED to S5d** and no longer blocks S5c's cap work. The substantive S5c
findings in `ec92508` are closed. Formal approval of the plan artifact remains
**HOLD** only until a fix-forward docs commit replaces the stale pending note
at `plan:2215` with the binding S5d contract:

- `prompt_id` on every prompt-scoped delta, message, tool call, result, and
  error, while helper-wide `session:null` errors remain uncorrelated;
- exact active-id/streamed/capped clearing on result, session error, and
  session end, including Stop/interrupt behavior;
- an explicit reject-versus-drop policy for stale, missing, and future ids,
  including whether it counts toward the three-rejection restart and the
  invariant that it mutates no UI, state, timer, or queue;
- independent post-Stop/new-prompt stale delta, message, result, and error
  reds, including proof that no old frame releases a queued prompt early;
- the dependency/gate lines above, a named owner, red/green commits, and a
  real-binary private-Xvfb test through the production helper, native
  validator, and drawer.

The acceptance checklist was sent to BlackRobin as Agent Mail 6136. No
runtime gate was needed for this scope decision. The approved linear
push-through boundary remains the already-pushed **`da3028f`**.

## Secrets-window teardown investigation (Agent Mail 6183)

### Status: OPEN (GNOME Shell crash probable path not captured)

BlueBeaver could not reproduce the user's GNOME Shell 48.7 `BadWindow`
session loss in 57 private-Xvfb attempts, including idle, in-flight and
code-entry Secrets states and WM close, SIGTERM and SIGKILL variants. The
private shell did not exercise a real clipboard-manager handoff, however, and
Copy link preceded the user's crash. Therefore neither root cause nor a fix
for the GNOME Shell crash has been proved.

The experiment did expose an independent lifecycle defect worth fixing as
defense in depth: GTK removes `WM_TRANSIENT_FOR`, destroys the parent, then
leaves the mapped Secrets window orphaned for roughly 80–150 ms; its destroy
handler never runs, so an in-flight sign-in is not cancelled. I approved a
follow-up plan/red/green after S6b1 Part B that destroys Secrets before its
parent, cancels exactly once, leaves no window behind, and covers the case
where another browser window survives. Approval of that change must not be
reported as closure of the GNOME Shell crash unless a reproducer or equivalent
mechanism evidence connects it. The ruling was sent in Agent Mail 6184.

### `a55d854` — APPROVED

quit, requires exactly-once cancellation, and names the SIGTERM ordering gap.

### `789b4f1` — BLOCKED-for-tests

The X-event observer and five cases are the correct test shape, but two harness
errors can misidentify or miss the very windows whose lifetime they claim to
pin:

- `two_windows()` returns `before.pop()` and then evaluates
  `(after - before).pop()`. Evaluation is left-to-right, so the first operation
  empties `before`; the second can select either browser window. Compute both
  identities from unchanged sets, assert each is unique, then return them.
- `other-closes` attempts a post-close drain with `until=set()`, but
  `collect()` exits immediately because the empty set is already a subset of
  `gone`. Thus a delayed parent/Secrets unmap or destroy is not observed.
  `xinput.toplevels()` checks title/geometry, not map state, so its later query
  does not close the gap. Add a real time-bounded/quiet-window drain and assert
  the two windows remain mapped.

gate and lands before the Part-B-dependent green. The findings were sent in
Agent Mail 6188. The approved linear push-through boundary remains the
already-pushed **`da3028f`**.

## S6b1 Part-B production green (`b499cd7`)

### `b499cd7` — APPROVED for code; user-screen Part B remains pending

The production change closes the red chain `e53d931` + `72eaaef` without
bypassing it:

- the one-shot helper derives `HTTPS_PROXY` and `HTTP_PROXY` from the
  `SandboxBackend` egress endpoint used by chat, keeps only loopback in
  `NO_PROXY`, and the real-binary proxy case crosses the login sandbox, login
  netd, outer relay, native login supervisor, Secrets window and token store;
- the exchange clock begins only when the helper writes a code to the CLI,
  is cleared when the CLI presents a new code prompt, and is subordinate to
  the existing ten-minute whole-login deadline. Post-code OAuth/retry output
  becomes the fixed `exchange` ending, while pre-code copies remain inert;
- `exchange` is admitted by the exact native login-frame validator. The C
  layer sees only its code, maps every ending to a fixed sentence, and never
  renders or logs the helper's message or PTY output; and
- the error path remains exactly-once, stops/reaps the helper, stores no token,
  and a retry hides the old reason before beginning a new sign-in.

- clean-export, display-free `test_login_exchange.py`: **9/9 passed**;
- clean-export private-Xvfb `agent_login_exchange_test.py` through the real

classified as post-code under extreme scheduling. The committed pre-code

## WKWebView routed-command port and WS0.7 fix-forward at `2b3b242`

### macOS MS2a.1 green (`dbf74b5`)

**`dbf74b5` is BLOCKED.** The two-host success route crosses the authenticated
socket, engine, macOS PagePort, named `WKContentWorld`, and live DOM; returned
C strings are paired with `zb_automation_free`. The production bridge does not
yet satisfy the PagePort's deadline and navigation contracts:

- `src/wkwebview_shim.m:901-903` ignores the kick wait result and can dispatch
  `loadRequest` after the waiter has returned. `:999-1002` similarly allows a
  late async-JavaScript completion to write and allocate after return, while
  `zb_auto_await` ignores its backstop result at `:850-851`. These are exposed
  production paths, so the no-dispatch/no-write guard cannot safely wait for a
  later ownership slice.
- `navigate_guarded` treats the shared `finishedOrFailed` bit as success for
  both outcomes and the delegate exits the whole app on failure. It therefore
  cannot produce the required `NavigationFailed`, and an old load completion
  can satisfy a newer navigation. Each load needs owned generation/result
  state.
- the vtable advertises `navigateWithPolicy`, but the shim discards
  `before_unload` at `:878-884`, contrary to the current MS2a.1 inventory.
- the timeout test exercises only startup `page.title` and permits an 800 ms
  request to take almost 6 seconds. It does not cover a blocked main queue,
  never-settling eval, late effects, failed/stale navigation, or the author's
  observed never-responding `page.navigate` hang.
- the registered gate reuses the still-blocked `stop_browser_macos`: it returns
  when the leader has exited without signaling a surviving saved process group.

Static shell, Zig-format and diff checks pass. The Linux gate was not run
because another owner held the slot. Findings were sent to JadeBeacon in Agent
Mail 6227. The partial gate should be named MS2a.1 (or remain unregistered)
until MS2a.2/3 close the plan's single MS2a gate.

### WS0.7 field-source design (`2b3b242`)

**`2b3b242` is NOT APPROVED — needs revision before implementation.** Its
strict-current-policy and PID-aware direction are preferable to a port-range
bypass, but four boundary contracts are incomplete:

1. The scheduled-task `console_user` JSON has no exact path, owner/ACL,
   atomic-publish, freshness or per-run challenge contract. A stale or
   test-user-writable file can falsely attest that the console is safe.
2. Effective write access is not “Allow minus Deny” over `Get-Acl`; it combines
   ordered/inherited NTFS ACEs, token groups and share permissions. Require a
   Windows `AccessCheck`-equivalent result or an explicitly proven read-only
   baseline whose share list, share ACL and NTFS ACL fingerprints are all
   revalidated without modifying served data.
3. The firewall digest omits security-relevant fields such as Enabled,
   RemoteAddress, Interface/Profile details, Program/Service and edge traversal,
   and does not define locale/encoding/parser refusal. Specify a canonical
   schema and hash the entire relevant policy; parsing failure must be an
   unavailable value that the gate rejects.
4. PID alone is reusable and “owned a listener before” lets any pre-existing
   process open a new persistent high port. Bind ownership to process creation
   identity/path/service and a reviewed allowlist, and version the listener
   schema when changing from integers to objects so producer and validator
   cannot silently disagree.

The proposed production-box provisioning remains correctly deferred until the
user/orchestrator is awake and explicitly authorizes it.

## macOS native-click spike at `a0c4a80`

**BLOCKED.** The two-host real-socket proof establishes the useful core fact:
an in-process `NSEvent` reaches WKWebView as a trusted click on both Mac
architectures. Moving the first `WKContentWorld` lookup onto the main queue also
fixes a credible off-main WebKit initialization trap. The commit nevertheless
wires `nativeClick` into the production PagePort while knowingly omitting the
PagePort/ABI safety contract:

1. `src/wkwebview_shim.m:1029-1067` ignores the backstop semaphore result. If
   the main queue stays blocked through the caller's timeout, the caller returns
   while the queued block remains able to dispatch down/up later. Timeout must
   revoke an atomic waiter claim that the main-thread job must win before its
   first event.
2. `:1027-1030` discards `expected_doc`, even though the shared ABI requires a
   same-callback token comparison and zero events on mismatch. A navigation can
   therefore redirect a click to replacement content.

   error. A terminated or unresponsive WebProcess can be reported as a
   successfully acknowledged click.
4. The partial click test is unregistered and covers trusted delivery only. It
   does not drive timeout abandonment, document replacement, per-window
   routing, failed readiness or ack failure through the production chain.

The capability must remain unwired until these invariants are red/green, or

blockers remain open. Formal findings were sent in Agent Mail 6253.

**BLOCKED; this does not close `d2bd016`'s pinned-use contract.** The new

   refused. No `\\.\C:\...` red exists.

### macOS eval ownership bridge (`93d925c`)

**BLOCKED.** The heap job removes caller-stack result writes and discards a
completion which arrives after abandonment, but it does not yet provide the
claimed no-dispatch-after-timeout guarantee.

1. BLOCKER: `wkwebview_shim.m:1094-1116` checks `zb_job_running(jref)` and
   later submits `callAsyncJavaScript` as two separate operations. The waiter
   can set `ABANDONED` at `:936` after the check at `:1097` but before the
   submission at `:1112`; the ABI then returns timeout before page code with
   possible side effects is dispatched. Claiming the job on the poll's first
   main-thread run protects only work that never began. Submission needs an
   explicit locked phase/handshake: a timeout may cancel preflight, but cannot
   return while the main thread is between its final ownership decision and
   the synchronous async-call submission.
2. BLOCKER-for-tests: the commit contains no deterministic regression which
   pauses at that exact check-to-submit boundary, expires the waiter, resumes
   the main thread and proves that the evaluated function never ran. The
   reported routed and timeout Mac gates exercise eval, but cannot kill this
   race.
3. BLOCKER: `:853-860` increments the live count and dereferences an unchecked
   `calloc` result. More importantly, `build.zig:1804` compiles this file with
   `-fobjc-arc`; Apple dispatch objects participate in ARC, and the unqualified
   `dispatch_semaphore_t` field is strong. `zb_job_unref` at `:870-879` frees
   malloc-backed storage without first deinitializing that strong field. ARC
   does not automatically destroy objects in malloc storage: the field must be
   cleared (or an equivalent explicit ownership design used) before `free`.
   The current code therefore leaks the semaphore and violates the ARC storage
   lifetime rule even though the job counter decrements. Add a Mac regression
   which observes dispatch-object release, not only `zb_auto_live_jobs`.

private-Xvfb slot. Findings were sent to JadeBeacon in Agent Mail 6298; the ARC
lifetime item was corrected from SHOULD to BLOCKER with the Clang/libdispatch

## S6 teardown, authorization and exchange batch

### Secrets-window teardown (`34a973d`)

**APPROVED.** `zb_secrets_window_present` now gives the transient its GTK
`destroy-with-parent` relationship and installs a weak-parent `delete-event`
handler (`src/agent_secrets_window.c:813-846`). A close-button path therefore
destroys Secrets before allowing the parent close to continue; other parent
destruction lets GTK destroy it with the parent. The existing Secrets destroy
handler increments the epoch, wipes pending material and calls the idempotent
login cancellation path (`:678-689`), so a running sign-in receives its one
ending. Re-presenting against another browser window disconnects and removes
the old weak-parent relationship before installing the new one.

The registered real-binary Xvfb test drives idle close, in-code close,
SIGTERM, unrelated-window close and parent-close-with-a-surviving-window. Its
quiet-window and map-state assertions preserve the `6b50712` fixes and kill
the three reported lifetime mutants. The prior diagnostic SHOULD remains:
the test's direct `XGetWindowAttributes` query has no local BadWindow trap, so
a disappearance race can terminate the runner rather than return a clean
false. This does not false-green the lifecycle contract.

This is still defense in depth, **not closure of the GNOME Shell 48.7
BadWindow crash**. Its mechanism was never reproduced and remains open, as
both the commit and test state explicitly.

### App-owned authorization-URL check (`225316a`)

**APPROVED.** `agent_auth.authorizeUrl` enforces the authoritative complete
URL grammar before use: at most 4096 visible-ASCII bytes, exact HTTPS
host/path pairs, no user info/port/fragment, all eight raw/plain parameter
names exactly once, the five fixed values, lowercase UUID client id,
43-character base64url challenge and nonempty state
(`src/agent_auth.zig:42-111`). `zb_login_validate` invokes it at the native
login-frame boundary (`src/agent_login.zig:102-106`), before
`agent_login.c` can deliver an `AUTH_URL` event to the Secrets or future auth
window. A rejection therefore follows the existing fixed `error-protocol`
path rather than exposing or loading the URL.

One fixture table drives the direct Zig check, the exported native validator
and Python helper parity. It includes exact 4096/4097 edges, raw encoded-name
aliases/duplicates, controls/NUL/space/non-ASCII, every fixed value and unique
case names. The one malformed-escape helper difference is declared and
bounded. This cumulatively closes the test blockers on `ed2a2cd`, `4397030`
and `2d7ea89`.

### CLI-consumption exchange boundary (`522f252`)

**APPROVED.** After writing a code, the helper now makes OAuth/retry text
eligible only after the first eight-or-more-star masked echo at or after the
write offset (`agent/host/zb_agent_host/login.py:241-248`). A new prompt still
stops the exchange clock before answering it, a missing echo still reaches
the existing 60-second timeout, and neither CLI text nor a token is added to
an error frame. The second failing-first case separates the echo from the
eventual token by one second, so taking the boundary at the helper's old read
offset cannot pass accidentally. The bare retry fake now mirrors the real
CLI's masked echo. This closes the red `b850544` and the earlier exchange
boundary SHOULD.

### S6b2 auth-test seam decision (`0f60910`)

**APPROVED for the S6b2 seam-decision slice.** This does not claim the auth
window or its TLS/proxy wiring. `authTestSeam` returns `none` when unset and

When active it accepts only the exact loopback-HTTP decimal-port grammar and

## Recovered review draft after the 2026-10-20 worktree-deletion incident

At approximately 07:43 EDT, another agent's cleanup script expanded an unset
path and executed a bare `find -delete` from the shared checkout. The checkout,
its `.git` link and this uncommitted review draft were deleted. The orchestrator
restored the index at `b804f9a`; the branch subsequently advanced as normal.

verdicts. The cited mail bodies are the canonical detailed record if this
condensed recovery and a mail ever differ.

RoseCat's own cleanup audit found no persistent cleanup script to restore. All
future throwaway cleanup commands must validate their target and spell it as,
for example, `find "${D:?}" -delete`; a bare `find -delete` is prohibited.
The first post-restore status check found implementer-owned S7 bridge work in
progress. It was preserved untouched.

### Post-recovery review: macOS MS2c FIFO and opener identity

#### `f136b35` — per-window FIFO regression

**BLOCKED-for-tests.** The scenario is directionally correct: two independent
socket clients address different stable `window_id` lines, the popup's missing
selector should occupy one line for four seconds, and the primary should remain
usable. It also correctly avoids freezing a potentially shared WebProcess.

The ordering premise is not observed, however. The test starts `hit_popup()` on
a Python thread and sleeps 200 ms before issuing the primary request. Nothing
proves the popup request has reached and entered its FIFO before the primary
request is sent. A serialized implementation can therefore pass if the new
thread is delayed and the primary wins the race; the later `elapsed >= 2`
sanity check proves only that the popup request eventually waited, not that it
was already ahead of the primary. Add an observable start barrier on the real
queue/operation path (or a deterministic mutant which globally serializes page
lines and is killed by this exact test) before using this test to close the
per-window independence edge. The `FROZEN popup` comments are also inaccurate;
the test deliberately uses a healthy popup with a retrying selector.

#### `4b914ec` — stable two-hop opener identity

**APPROVED.** This is the missing discriminator from the `a455e30` review. Two
throwaway popups make registry position diverge from the monotonic stable id;
the real two-hop primary → A → B chain then requires B's opener to equal A's
stable id. Closing middle window A verifies that B's id and its frozen opener
survive and that the dead opener id is not a surviving window. The URL-settle
poll removes the page-list-before-commit race without weakening identity
assertions. The reported index-derived-opener mutant fails only the new chain,
which is the intended failing-first evidence. The only source change is the
corrected API comment; no production behavior changes.

### Post-recovery review: drawer plan rev 16.20.32 (`3f923f2`)

**APPROVED.** This closes the four plan blockers recorded in Agent Mail 6513:

- `tool_result` now has an exact success/error union, preserves ordered text
  and PNG/JPEG image blocks, rejects unknown or cross-variant fields and bad
  base64, bounds the line, forgets the call id on malformed input and prevents
  malformed content from reaching the model;
- S7a owns the bounded broker deadline `B = H - min(5, H/4)`, specifies one
  terminal result, drains the worker after timeout and pins both endpoint
  budgets plus the late-engine race;
- result, session failure, Stop, window-close/end-session, shutdown and stdin
  EOF all end pending calls exactly once, with ids forgotten before
  `session_ended`, and the forced-order tests cover result/end, timeout/result
  and a late old-prompt result against a new prompt;
- the frame tables now carry `prompt_id` on every prompt-scoped frame and the
  plan explicitly says S7.0/S7a are increments, while S7 acceptance still
  requires S7b's real-binary closure tests.

The implementation must still make the one-MiB rule's byte-count boundary
match the framing reader exactly, but the plan's exact-boundary reds are the
right place to enforce that; it is not a remaining plan blocker.

Agent Mail 6552.

### WebView2 WS3 marshal (`c4e713a`, `f762094`, `61dfbe3`)

- **`c4e713a` APPROVED** as the failing-first regression. The test creates a
  real queued job, holds it before its commit point until the waiter expires,
  and proves the cookie write never runs. Its parked callback also drives a
  genuinely in-flight read across loop termination and then delivers the late
  completion.
- **`f762094` APPROVED.** `QUEUED -> RUNNING` is one interlocked ownership
  transition; pre-claim abandonment cannot run. Running jobs are tracked under
  the jobs lock, loop end drains queued and in-flight sets, and
  `RUNNING -> COMPLETING` grants exactly one writer of result/error before the
  DONE event. Callback references keep late completions alive, and the waiter
  handles the COMPLETING race by waiting for publication. This closes the
  timeout, in-flight-loop-end and double-completer blockers from the `15fb6ee`
  review.
- **`61dfbe3` APPROVED.** The history document now describes the shipped
  state machine and 400-day WebView2 cookie cap, while honestly leaving the
  owner-only profile DACL to WS2.0's shared `restrictToOwner` work.

45/45 and loop-end mutant 2 failures. Agent Mail 6553.

### MS2c view-replacement recovery (`5efa5dd`)

**BLOCKED.** Replacing a WKWebView is a viable public-API recovery mechanism,
the host preserves its stable id/opener/process-group metadata, and the
existing two-phase queue/consent flow remains in production. The implementation
has two old-view lifetime violations, however:

1. `recoverByReplacingWebView` clears `pendingDialogKind` without answering or
   releasing the held alert/confirm/prompt completion. Close/dealloc explicitly
   documents that WebKit requires those completions to be called. The stale
   block remains retained while kind is zero; a later dialog can release it
   uncalled, and close/dealloc will skip it. Answer any pending dialog through
   `zbRespondDialogAccept:NO` before detaching the old delegate, and add a real
   two-phase recovery test with an open dialog.
2. `healthTick` captures the old view for its JavaScript ping, but the callback
   checks only weak `self`. A late old-view reply after replacement can clear

**BLOCKED.** Selecting the primary view's `WKHTTPCookieStore`, copying native

remain:

## Exact closure routes for the WS0 claim at `1b58f85`

The standard is not relaxed, but the old commit subject need not force a false
milestone claim forever. Either of these fix-forward routes is acceptable.

### Route A: prove full WS0 green

1. On Linux, from a clean export with no real display, the production gate
   selftest must exit zero with `Ran 15 tests ... OK`, and the two-host
   selftest must exit zero with `Ran 17 tests ... OK`. A bounded private-Xvfb
   full gate must then report an all-green literal `Build Summary`; both named
   Windows selftest steps must actually run.
2. Against the real Win11 VM through the Linux driver,
   `tests/windows/resolve_live_test.py` must not skip and must exit zero with
   exact output `PASS live resolver regression ASSERTS 2`.
3. Against both pinned Windows hosts, the production probe/gate must first be
   completed so every WS0.1–WS0.8 field is produced and validated fail closed.
   Today that condition does not hold: `interactive_session` and `locked` are
   null; the probe omits `console_user`, `shares`, `zbtest_write_paths`,
   `fw_rules_hash`, and `snapshot_marker`; and the gate does not validate the
   complete readiness schema. A bounded `gate.sh --probe-only` must then exit
   zero with empty stderr and exactly one `WIN11 <JSON>` plus one
   `WIN10 <JSON>` stdout line. Both objects must satisfy the plan, the Win10
   pre/post listener and firewall values must be unchanged, and the
   orchestrator must watch the first run and confirm the reported interactive
   session is the one on the monitor.

For reference, the two current Linux suites independently produced **15/15**
and **17/17**, both `OK`, with all display variables removed. That is necessary
foundation evidence, not the missing Windows evidence.

### Route B: narrow the delivered scope to the Linux foundation

This route **is acceptable** under the review rules. A new authoritative docs
fix-forward may explicitly supersede the old subject and classify `1b58f85`,
`b8dcd21`, and `3097d78` as **WS0 Linux foundation only**, provided it:

- cites the 15-test Linux result plus an all-green clean-export/private-Xvfb

No Windows-host run is required to accept that deliberately narrow foundation.

## Follow-up review at `927cb4d`: S7b green and remaining prompt guards

Both diffs are whitespace-clean. The changed Python module compiles and the
guest shell script passes `bash -n`. No full gate was taken; BlackRobin owns
the current slot and reported only the focused S7b suites for this green.

### S7b broker green (`1925787`)

**BLOCKED.** The ordinary paths are sound: `replyOf` makes result/error
exclusive and redacts genuine errors; `window_info` validates its typed health
entry and obtains URL/title from their own calls; `Outcome` owns bytes through
the synchronous sink call; worker and deadline publication share the broker
mutex with detach; queued calls are dropped; and the registered reds plus the
reported nine mutants discriminate the intended behavior.

The allocation-failure path breaks the defining lifetime rule. At
`src/agent_broker.zig:314-321`, `Reaper.adopt` appends the broker to an
allocating list. If that append fails, it unlocks and calls `broker.reap()` on
the caller. The caller is the GTK close path, and `reap()` joins the worker and
timer; a running engine call may need GTK to finish. Thus OOM recreates the
exact main-thread deadlock that the reaper exists to prevent.

Make adoption allocation-free (an intrusive broker link is one suitable
shape), or otherwise ensure no failure path joins/frees the live broker on the
GTK caller. Add an allocation-failure red with a running GTK-dependent call:
detach still returns within the bound, then off-thread reaping leaves no sink,
thread or allocation. A clean descendant full gate remains required after the
fix. Finding sent to BlackRobin in Agent Mail 6650.

### Remaining real SSH/SCP prompt guards (`927cb4d`)

**APPROVED.** The MSI e2e puts `BatchMode=yes` in both independently built
SSH and SCP argv lists. The guest script puts it in the shared SSH argv that
SCP reuses. `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never` is defense in depth; BatchMode is the
decisive noninteractive control. Fake-SSH-only selftests correctly need no
change. Verdict sent to AzureRidge in Agent Mail 6651.

## Follow-up review at `d0adb84`: allocation-free broker reaping and MS3 cleanup

Both reviewed ranges are whitespace-clean, and the changed macOS Python test

### Broker OOM detach red (`8cf8d05`)

**APPROVED as the failing-first red.** The test supplies a fail-at-first-use
allocator to the production `Reaper`, holds a real broker call inside the fake
engine, and invokes `detach` on a helper so the old synchronous join becomes a
bounded test failure rather than hanging the runner. On `1925787`, the failed
list append reaches `broker.reap()` on that caller and cannot return before the
held call is released; owner evidence records `TestNotReached`. After release,
the test also requires no sink call, reaper completion, baseline thread count
and allocator cleanliness.

**SHOULD-for-tests:** assert the no-late-sink count again after
`reaper.deinit()` has joined all broker threads. That is a causal endpoint and
does not need the current 300 ms sleep. The `<50 ms` timing assertion is also
load-sensitive and redundant with the stronger fact that detach returned
within the outer bound while the engine remained held.

### Allocation-free intrusive Reaper (`d0adb84`)

**Production code APPROVED; final acceptance BLOCKED-on-gate only.**
`Broker.reap_next` makes the reaper queue intrusive. `Reaper.adopt` now performs
only pointer mutations under its mutex; it has no allocator and therefore no
failure path that can call `Broker.reap()` on the GTK caller. If thread spawn
fails, the broker stays owned by the list, a later adoption retries spawning,
and shutdown `deinit` drains it after the GTK loop. The worker pops under the
same mutex and still performs the potentially blocking joins off that mutex.

The OOM red is registered in the ordinary S7 test set. Reported focused results
are OOM 1/1 (three repeats), detach 3/3, broker 11/11, reply 8/8, window-info
2/2, in-process 5/5 and server 55/55. Restoring caller-side reap makes the OOM
red fail. Finding 6650 explicitly required a clean descendant full gate after
the fix; that gate had not completed at review time, so it is the sole remaining
acceptance condition. Verdict sent to BlackRobin in Agent Mail 6665.

**APPROVED.** The stale “unregistered” label is removed. After a browser is
created, every normal or exceptional exit from the test body closes the RPC,
stops the browser process group, and only then removes its per-launch socket
directory. This closes the ordinary leak from finding 6643. The reported MS3
gate is green on x86_64 and arm64. A failure of `subprocess.Popen` itself could
