## macOS Keychain owner follow-up (`d0ea97b`)

**BLOCKED.** The optional pointer, pointer-taking deinit, and second deinit on
the same variable correctly close one half of `f6b005b`: one owner is disarmed
after release. The code and test do not close the stale-copy defect that the
comments claim to solve. `Token` remains a freely copyable public value; a
copy made while its pointer is live keeps the same non-null pointer after the
original is deinitialized, and deinitializing that copy frees the allocation
again. The new regression never copies a live owner.

The implementation also assigns null only after calling the C free function,
not with the requested take-and-null-before-free ordering, and calling the
field “internal” is not an enforced Zig visibility boundary. Fix forward with
either a genuinely alias-safe shared release handle, or an honest unique-owner
API: remove the stale-copy safety claim, minimize raw-field exposure, disarm
before the C call, and pin the never-copy rule across all production callers.
No production consumer is wired yet, so this can be settled before the API is
depended upon. Finding sent to JadeBeacon in Agent Mail 6733.

## Windows live-resolver regression hardening (`7751e6e`)

**APPROVED.** The live regression now removes ambient `ZB_RESOLVE_CMD` from
the production gate's environment, pins the same Win11 port, key and

count the negative unless `fsutil reparsepoint query` first succeeds and
identifies `C:\\Windows` as the junction target. Thus a missing junction, an

### MS5 parent-death fix-forward (`7d06792`)

**BLOCKED on one remaining check/register race.** Making setup the process
group leader, forbidding its macOS descendants from changing group, having its
own watcher `killpg(..., SIGKILL)`, and censusing every group member and
descendant after SIGKILLing the browser correctly address the ordinary
unhandled-death hole. But the plan checks `getppid()` once and only then
registers `EVFILT_PROC/NOTE_EXIT`. A browser death between those operations can
be missed. The contract must treat registration/kevent failure as parent death
and re-check the expected parent immediately after successful registration;
the e2e needs a barrier/mutant for that exact window followed by the same
zero-group census. Item 4 and the bundled-Python addendum remain separate
holds. Finding sent in Agent Mail 6773.

### MS5 parent-death plan closure (`7d06792`, `9d299bd`)

**`7d06792` is cumulatively APPROVED by `9d299bd`; `9d299bd` is APPROVED.**
The final plan now makes setup the process-group leader, installs a Darwin
`EVFILT_PROC`/`NOTE_EXIT` watch before setup does other work, treats every
registration and wait error as parent death, and rechecks the captured parent
PID after successful registration. That closes both ordinary SIGKILL cleanup
and the check-to-register/reused-PID race. Every death path kills setup's own
group, while ordinary browser shutdown also kills and reaps it.

The test contract is appropriately split: a real both-architecture e2e holds
between the first parent check and registration, SIGKILLs the browser and
requires a zero-member/zero-descendant census within two seconds; an injected
Linux unit test covers the otherwise impractical reused-PID interleaving and
registration-error mutants. Item 4's file-owner approval and the separate
bundled-Python corrections remain independent MS5 holds; they do not reopen
this item-5 verdict. No executable code changed in these two plan commits.

### `7e0a9bf` — BLOCKED; do not run it on Win10 yet

The commit correctly removes explicit remote script staging: `probe_host`
streams `host_probe.ps1` into one SSH process, and `probe_only` invokes that
path for the Win10 pre/post probes with the Win10 key and known-hosts
arguments. There is no Win10 `scp`, remote redirection, mkdir, cleanup or
result file in that call graph. The separate known-hosts values retain
`StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`. The Win11 VM threshold is correctly 10 GiB while
the file-server threshold remains 20 GiB. The targeted hostless suite is
green, **53/53 tests**, and the shell/Python syntax checks pass.

However, transport without a staged file is not a zero-write execution. The
streamed script executes `Add-Type -MemberDefinition` at
`tests/windows/host_probe.ps1:12-21`. Windows PowerShell 5.1 implements that
dynamic compilation through .NET Framework CodeDOM temporary compiler files,
even though the resulting assembly is loaded in memory. PowerShell's own
[#7914](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/7914) records the
write-access dependency; the .NET Framework compiler path uses a
`TempFileCollection` and deletes those artifacts only after compilation.
That violates the user's literal rule that this gate writes nothing on the
physical Win10 file server.

The new test at `tests/windows/gate_twohost_selftest.py:513-530` does not catch
this: fake SSH records stdin and returns canned JSON; it never executes the
PowerShell script. It proves only the absence of `-File` and presence of the
streamed bytes. Before the first live run, add a Win10-specific probe path with
no dynamic compilation or other write-capable primitive, plus a failing-first
contract proving that the file-server route selects it while retaining the
exact stdin oracle. The stale header at `host_probe.ps1:2` should also name the
actual `$input | Out-String | iex` command rather than `powershell -Command -`.

## WS0 zero-write Win10 probe fix-forward (`0353dfb`)

Reviewed at `0353dfb` on 2026-10-20 17:56 EDT.

**Verdict: APPROVED.** This closes the `7e0a9bf` blocker recorded in review
commit `9875e1b`; the watched first live two-host `--probe-only` run may
proceed.

The Win10 route still consists only of the SSH process reading the exact
`host_probe.ps1` bytes from stdin and returning JSON on stdout. Both pre and
post calls use the Win10 key argument and its own known-hosts file. No staging,
`scp`, remote file redirection, result file, mkdir or cleanup command is in
that call graph.

The execution path is now genuinely different from the blocked version:

- `host_probe.ps1:16-36` creates an assembly with
  `AssemblyBuilderAccess.Run`. Microsoft defines that access as executable but
  **not savable**.
- It calls the one-argument `DefineDynamicModule(String)` overload, which
  Microsoft defines as a **transient** module. It supplies no output filename,
  never selects `RunAndSave`, and never calls `Save`.
- There is no `Add-Type`, CodeDOM, `csc`, source compilation or compiler temp
  path. The three P/Invoke signatures are metadata emitted into that transient
  module. Native architecture and the SSH process's session id now use managed
  runtime properties.
- A command-by-command audit of the remainder found only registry/file/ACL
  reads, DriveInfo, WTS reads, `netstat`/`netsh` queries, in-memory hashing and
  JSON stdout. There is no filesystem or registry mutation primitive.

The exact-commit clean-export run is green: **55/55** two-host selftests,
`bash -n`, and an independent assertion of the `Run` plus transient-module
shape. The prior `Add-Type` source necessarily fails the new scanner. The
corrected shared-private-key default plus distinct known-hosts default matches
the configured hosts.

**SHOULD, not a live-run blocker:** broaden the source regression so future
mutants using `RunAndSave`, `.Save`, the filename-bearing
`DefineDynamicModule` overload, `FileStream`/`File.Create`, directory
creation, Copy/Move/Remove/Rename, `Start-Transcript` or `Tee-Object` also
fail. The current source is clean, but the present deny list does not name all
of those spellings. Also update `gate.sh:145-149`, whose comment still
describes the removed Add-Type here-string.

## WS0 field-validation hardening (`f766655`)

Reviewed at `f766655` on 2026-10-20 18:03 EDT.

**Verdict: BLOCKED.** This fix-forward correctly closes part of finding 6799:
the VM and file-server roots are exact, empty share identities are refused,
port 22 is required, the pinned snapshot name is updated and its creation time
must parse, and the plan explicitly defers VM Python/Zig and the file-server
WebView2 value to the slices that actually use them. The exact-commit clean
export passes all **65/65** hostless two-host tests plus `bash -n`.

Four fail-closed holes remain:

1. `tests/windows/gate.sh:258-263` only rejects an empty SSH listen list and a
   short wildcard blacklist. The plan pins `ListenAddress 100.123.34.15`, but
   a focused production-path call with `sshd_listen=["192.0.2.44"]` exits 0.
   Require typed strings and the exact configured tailnet address.
2. `gate.sh:213-220` requires only nonempty share-name/path strings. A share
   `{name:"docs", path:"relative\\docs"}` exits 0. Finding 6799 required
   absolute normalized roots and explicit duplicate/alias behavior; add those
   validators and mutants. The WS0.7 baseline is also specified as listeners
   22, 135, 139, 445 and 3389, but the gate requires only 22, so both probes
   can omit the other four and still pass.
3. `host_probe.ps1:182-190` ORs every applicable Allow mask, ORs every Deny
   mask, then subtracts the latter. This is per-bit but not Windows access-check
   semantics: AccessCheck processes ACEs sequentially and can stop when the
   requested right is granted or denied. In particular, an explicit Allow can
   satisfy a right before a later inherited Deny, while this aggregate removes
   the bit and unsafely reports the path read-only. The new tests feed canned
   JSON and never execute the ACL calculation; the required allow/deny/order
   and individual-right PowerShell oracle is still absent.
4. Numeric narrowing is still incomplete. Python's JSON decoder accepts NaN,
   and both VM and file-server `free_gb=NaN` exit 0 because `NaN < limit` is
   false. Require a finite real number. Both focused survivors were exercised
   through the real `gate.sh --probe-only` validator, not a copied helper.

No live Windows host, full gate, browser or display was used. Findings were
mailed to AzureRidge in Agent Mail 6822.

## macOS plan rev 15 (`b4ec5e9`)

Reviewed at `b4ec5e9` on 2026-10-20 18:03 EDT.

**Verdict: BLOCKED as an implementation-ready plan.** Rev 15 correctly records
the measured SHA-256 and the Sigstore signer identity/issuer, excludes
`python3.12-intel64` plus its link from the bundle and census, and pins the fat
`bin/python3.12` interpreter with no macOS venv. Those are the right resolutions
for most of finding 6770.

The acquisition contract is internally inconsistent. Lines 1324-1329 record
SHA-256 and Sigstore, but lines 1330-1333 still direct the build to verify only
the Apple package signature and **MD5** before unpacking. They neither compare
the SHA-256 nor verify the downloaded `.sigstore` bundle against
`thomas@python.org` and `https://accounts.google.com`. The official Python
3.12.10 release page publishes the MD5 and links the Sigstore artifact; it does
not publish the SHA-256, so line 1325 also misattributes the independently
measured hash to that page.

Fix forward by making SHA-256 the mandatory byte-integrity check, making the
Sigstore bundle's identity and issuer a mandatory verification step with a
named command/seam, retaining `pkgutil --check-signature`/notarization as the
Apple package check, and treating MD5 as informational only. The slice needs
failing-first oracles for wrong SHA-256, missing/wrong Sigstore bundle,
identity and issuer, plus survival of either excluded `*-intel64` entry in the
payload/census. Finding 6770 therefore remains open. The verdict was mailed to

## WS0 nonce trigger and field hardening (`6fa72c8`)

Reviewed at `6fa72c8` on 2026-10-20.

**Verdict: BLOCKED.** This fix-forward does close several concrete parts of
the `f766655` review: `sshd_listen` is now pinned to the configured address,
share identities are compared after Windows normalization and duplicates are
refused, `free_gb` must be finite, and the previously demonstrated
explicit-Allow-before-inherited-Deny case no longer gets flattened into
allow-minus-deny. The VM session path also now creates a per-run nonce,
triggers the console task and waits with a default 60-second deadline. In an
exact clean export the hostless suite is **75/75**, `bash -n` passes and the
diff is whitespace-clean. AzureRidge additionally reports a successful live
unlocked-VM trigger and four ad-hoc DACL cases.

The remaining blockers are:

1. `tests/windows/gate.sh:208-210` makes the plan's fixed file-server baseline
   `{22,135,139,445,3389}` replaceable through the ordinary ambient
   `ZB_WIN10_BASELINE_PORTS`. A focused invocation of the real
   `gate.sh --probe-only` validator with both probes reporting only port 22 and
   `ZB_WIN10_BASELINE_PORTS=22` exits **0**. This is not a fail-closed fixed
   baseline. Remove the production override, or confine any override to an
   unmistakable selftest-only seam whose inertness is tested.
2. `host_probe.ps1:166-204` is still not Windows AccessCheck. It treats every
   matching `FileSystemAccessRule` as effective and never inspects
   `PropagationFlags.InheritOnly`; Windows skips an inherit-only ACE on the
   object itself. It also does not account for the object owner's implicit
   `WRITE_DAC` right. Either omission can let an early non-effective Deny hide
   a later effective Allow, or can miss that the test user owns the served
   root and can grant itself write access, producing the unsafe empty
   `zbtest_write_paths`. Microsoft documents both rules in
   [ACE inheritance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/ace-inheritance-rules)
   and the
   [AccessCheck algorithm](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-dtyp/4f1bbcbb-814a-4c70-a11e-2a5b8779a6f9).
   Use the platform access-check primitive (or implement all of its applicable
   rules and fail closed on unsupported ACEs/null DACLs), and report/refuse an
   owned served root with mutable security.
3. No committed test executes that PowerShell ACL evaluator. The 75 hostless
   tests feed already-computed `zbtest_write_paths`; the reported live DACL
   cases are not a repeatable oracle. Add a Windows test over actual temporary
   DACLs which covers ACE order, an inherit-only ACE, ownership/implicit
   `WRITE_DAC`, each mutating right and an unreadable/unsupported descriptor.
   The old aggregate implementation and the current two unsafe mutants must
   turn it red.
4. The nonce tests at `gate_twohost_selftest.py:685-713` only find the strings
   `schtasks` and `nonce.txt`; their SSH stub emits a canned `RESULT=OK` and
   never runs `session_probe.ps1` or the nonce/freshness logic in
   `host_probe.ps1`. Thus deleting either nonce comparison survives. Moreover,
   `host_probe.ps1:141-143` checks only `ts > now-15m`: despite lines 131-132
   claiming otherwise, an arbitrarily future timestamp is accepted. Add a
   production-path Windows oracle for matching, mismatched, stale and future
   results, plus locked and unlocked desktops. The source still says
   `LIVE-VERIFY PENDING` for those latter states at
   `session_probe.ps1:13-14`.

**Contract/documentation gap:** `session_probe.ps1:5-7` says the gate installs
the helper/task, while the repository contains no task registration or script
staging path; `gate.sh:172` only triggers a pre-registered task. If this is an
external VM provisioning prerequisite, pin and verify the task name, action,
principal and script hash in the plan/gate. Otherwise a clean host cannot be

## WS0 real-file-server reconciliation and access oracle (`b620b51`)

Reviewed at `b620b51` on 2026-10-20 against the four open findings in
`50a4c5b` and the orchestrator's read-only observation of the real Windows 10
file server.

**Verdict: BLOCKED. Do not treat this as clearing WS0 for the first live
two-host `--probe-only` acceptance run.** The display-free hostless suite is
green **71/71**, `gate.sh` passes `bash -n`, the new Python compiles, and the
diff is whitespace-clean. Several real improvements land: the ambient
listener-baseline override is gone; pre/post listener equality remains; the
file-server root/free-space assumptions are correctly removed from code after
the orchestrator's observation; future-dated session evidence is refused;
and the committed test now executes the extracted production ACL and nonce
logic on the VM. Those close finding 1 and a material part of findings 3/4.

The remaining blockers are:

1. **The advertised Windows `AccessCheck` is still a hand-written
   approximation.** `host_probe.ps1:43-68` never calls `AccessCheck` and
   reduces the current token to `WindowsIdentity.User` plus the bare SIDs in
   `WindowsIdentity.Groups`. Windows access checking also consumes each
   token SID's attributes: disabled SIDs are ignored, while deny-only SIDs
   participate only in deny ACEs. An early deny ACE for a disabled group can
   therefore make this loop stop before a later effective allow and report a
   writable served path as read-only. It also cannot account for restricted
   token and privilege behavior. Microsoft's `AccessCheck` contract takes
   the security descriptor, client token, generic mapping and privilege set
   precisely for these semantics; a SID list is not equivalent. Use the real
   platform access check (a zero-disk Reflection.Emit P/Invoke is compatible
   with this probe) and fail closed if it cannot be performed.
2. **The committed ACL oracle is materially narrower than its claim and the
   required red.** `host_live_test.py:56-80` constructs in-memory
   `DirectorySecurity` objects, not actual temporary on-disk DACLs. Its
   scenarios exercise only `WriteData` and `Delete`; they do not independently
   cover `AppendData`, `DeleteSubdirectoriesAndFiles`, `ChangePermissions` or
   `TakeOwnership`, an unreadable/unsupported ACE, or enabled/disabled/
   deny-only token groups. The file is not registered by `build.zig`,
   `gate.sh`, or any Windows gate (`git grep` finds only comments), so the
   reported manual 5/5 is not repeatable gate evidence. Register it in the
   live Windows gate and make the old/manual evaluator and the missing token-
   attribute cases red.
3. **The externally provisioned task is not pin-verified as documented.** At
   `gate.sh:169-178`, `schtasks /FO LIST /V` is accepted if its localized free-
   form output contains `session_probe.ps1` anywhere and the current user's
   leaf name anywhere. That does not prove the exact action path, the run-as
   principal, `InteractiveToken`/“only when logged on,” or even which field
   supplied either substring. The hostless tests at
   `gate_twohost_selftest.py:647-690` only assert source substrings or inject
   a canned `RESULT`; the reported live 5/5 does not exercise a task mismatch.
   Query the task as XML and compare its action command/arguments, principal,
   logon type and enabled state field-by-field, with hostile-action, wrong-
   principal and noninteractive reds.
4. **The lock-state half of finding 4 remains explicitly unverified.** The
   new nonce cases plant `session.json` themselves; they prove that the real
   host probe accepts a matching/fresh record and drops mismatch, stale and
   far-future records, but they do not execute `session_probe.ps1`'s desktop
   detection. `session_probe.ps1:18-20` still records only an unlocked live
   observation and says the locked case is pending. A real locked-desktop
   run must produce `locked=true` before this signal is accepted.

The plan also contradicts the new decision in its authoritative text. The
new note at lines 523-529 says file-server `root`/`free_gb` and a fixed
listener baseline are not applicable, but lines 471-473 still require 20 GB
on that server, lines 713-714 still say its `free_gb` and `root` are gate-
enforced, and WS0.7 lines 748-754 still requires `free_gb` and the fixed
`22,135,139,445,3389` listener list. Reconcile the normative clauses rather
than leaving a later exception beside conflicting requirements.

No Windows host, file server, full gate, browser, live socket or display was
used locally. The official semantics checked during review are Microsoft's

## Chat drawer S8 approval design, rev 16.20.37 (`47e619b`)

Reviewed exact commit `47e619b` on 2026-10-20 against the threat model's
per-action approval invariant and the existing engine/flow boundaries.
**Verdict: BLOCKED.** The three questions sent to the user remain open and can
be decided independently; the findings below are defects in the proposed
security mechanism, not substitutes for those decisions.

1. **BLOCKER — story preview acts before approval.** Plan lines 3059 and 3088
   put all ten previews in the no-card set. Current `instagram.zig:311-313`
   and `:352-399` explicitly say that merely navigating to the story may mark
   the first frame seen. That is the action this approval protects. The story
   preview must be removed or made genuinely non-viewing, and a fixture red
   must show zero view/seen record before Approve.
2. **BLOCKER — revalidation is not atomic with the real ticket.** Line 3086's
   health/origin/load/account reads and the subsequent real call are separate
   `callInProcess` operations. Navigation or an account switch can occur after
   revalidation and before the real queue ticket. Raw DOM expects only
   `target_fp`, while navigate/reload have no target. Origin, `load_serial`,
   applicable account and dialog/crash validity must be checked after the real
   ticket is acquired and before any mutation. A deterministic hold in this
   gap must prove navigation/account change gives -32015 and zero input.
   `dialog_open` is currently read but not compared/refused.
3. **BLOCKER — the proposed fingerprint is cloneable semantics, not element
   identity.** Line 3075's tag/id/name/role/accessibility/text/frame fields are
   all reproducible on a replacement node. The isolated world needs an opaque,
   page-unforgeable per-element identity or an equivalent identity primitive,
   with a same-fields-clone red. Native/humanized input also needs a forced
   replacement after locate/pointer moves but before mouse-down; a check before
   the native sequence is not atomic with its event.
4. **BLOCKER — flows protect only their final click after earlier sensitive
   mutations.** Line 3084 leaves earlier click/fill/type/select steps
   unguarded. Current post/comment/message/DM/schedule flows type drafts,
   signal typing or select state before Send/Post, which can disclose content
   to a changed account/recipient even when the last click is refused. The
   grant must guard the account/recipient and every sensitive action target
   before the first and every later mutation in the same flow ticket. Tests
   must count zero input events, not only zero final fixture commits. The plan
   must also define the fingerprint source for `linkedin_message` and
   `instagram_dm`, which have no dry run.
5. **BLOCKER — Stop/prompt end does not revoke the card.** Line 3099 waits for
   session end but omits the active prompt ending and Stop. Bind a card/job to
   `prompt_id`; result, prompt-scoped error, Stop and `session_ended` must
   revoke it before a newer prompt can run. Force a stale Approve after Stop
   and after a new prompt and prove no dispatch.
6. **BLOCKER — the grant digest has no canonical encoding.** Line 3098 names
   `sha256(tool, ..., normalized_args)` but does not define field framing,
   JSON/key ordering, Unicode, numbers or absent versus null. Specify a typed,
   length-delimited/canonical representation and use the same immutable owned
   values for card display, digest and dispatch. Test delimiter, key-order and
   Unicode collision cases in addition to random one-field changes.
7. **BLOCKER-for-tests — the sole-minter statement lacks hostile-ingress
   proofs.** The named S8c/S8d reds do not directly prove that top page,
   same/cross-origin iframe, popup `zbHost`, socket client, helper frame/tool
   arguments and hook output cannot invoke approve/deny or mint a grant. Each
   ingress refusal needs a real negative and a removal mutant.
8. **BLOCKER-for-tests — approval state races are not linearized by the named
   suite.** A sequential second Approve does not cover Approve racing Deny,
   TTL, detach or prompt end. Deterministic races must yield one terminal
   `approvalend`, at most one dispatch, and no dispatch unless a still-valid
   Approve wins.

The separate gated-call budget and native-only mint direction are sound
starting points. Findings were mailed to BlackRobin, copied to JadeBeacon, in
Agent Mail 6913. The plan diff passes `git diff --check`. No test, display,
browser, live site or remote host was used for this docs-only review.

## MS6 Seatbelt profile-generator increment (`a4c07a2`)

Reviewed exact commit `a4c07a2` on 2026-10-20 against macOS plan rev 17,
MS6 and the shared `SandboxBackend` network capability. **Verdict: BLOCKED.**
The registered Linux suite passes 9/9, and the explicit `process-info*` deny,
filtered `sysctl-read` forms and hook-without-egress direction agree with the
measured MS6.1 belt. The renderer is not safe to consume, however:

1. **BLOCKER — generated-profile injection.** `sandbox_macos.py:49-51,68,74,77`
   interpolates paths and port-like values directly into Seatbelt source,
   contrary to the plan's required profile-file plus `-D` parameters. A
   quote/newline in `scratchpad` closes its filter and injects a new allow;
   `workspace` can escape its `;;` comment with a newline. A local probe using
   `scratchpad='/safe\")\n(allow file-write*)\n;;'` emitted that allow verbatim.
   Use named Seatbelt parameters (or a separately proved encoder where a
   parameter is impossible), reject hostile values, and add quote, slash,
   backslash, newline and parenthesis reds with a removal mutant.
2. **BLOCKER — an empty network policy becomes an unfiltered allow.** With
   `egress=None` and `bridges=()`, line 77 emits exactly
   `(allow network-outbound )`. A zero-endpoint capability must omit the allow
   or be refused; it must never broaden to every destination. Cover both CLI
   and hook empty-policy cases.
3. **BLOCKER — the rendered capability is not a checked projection of the
   backend value.** The code ignores `egress.host`, hardcodes `localhost`, and
   accepts arbitrary bridge values and port ranges. Require the exact loopback
   host and integer ports 1..65535, with fail-closed tests, so a malformed
   `LaunchSpec.network` cannot silently render a different policy.
4. **BLOCKER-for-tests — substring checks are not an independent profile
   oracle.** They do not reject the hostile input or empty-capability cases and
   do not establish that the generated profile parses. Add an independent
   static/profile-parameter oracle now; the required both-Mac `sandbox-exec`
   enforcement gate remains later.

The broad `file-read*` and blanket `mach-lookup` also do not meet final MS6
(`plan:1562-1566`). Because no production backend consumes this module yet and
the source labels that curation a later increment, they are recorded as
incomplete scope rather than a separate defect in this first increment. The
renderer must not be wired until deny-default reads and the tiny Mach lookup
set land.

## Chat drawer S8 approval design, rev 16.20.39 (`4a4c6d7`)

Reviewed exact docs commit `4a4c6d7` on 2026-10-20 against the five blockers
on rev 16.20.38 and the current automation implementation. **Verdict:
BLOCKED.** The new A/B/C load phases correctly stop comparing the old
document serial after the approved navigation; the document token binds later
steps to the new document; the nine-preview count and story-view exclusion now
agree; and the revision names concrete, fail-closed thread-header recipient
sources. Four security/contract gaps remain:

1. **BLOCKER — the claimed same-task atomicity ignores synchronous page event
   handlers.** `plan:3085-3091` says page script cannot interleave with the
   isolated-world task and checks an expectation once immediately before an
   action. In production, however, `automation.js:919-955` calls
   `dispatchEvent` repeatedly: click sends five events, type sends events per
   character, and fill/select send input then change. Each `dispatchEvent`
   synchronously runs the untrusted page's handlers before the function
   continues. A `pointerdown`, `keydown`, `beforeinput` or `input` handler can
   change the account/recipient or replace state before the later committing
   event, while the one pre-action check still passes. Define the guarded
   action primitive so it rechecks the document/account/recipient/target
   before every low-level event or mutation that follows a page callback, and
   add reds where a page handler changes each marker during `pointerdown` and
   during the first typed character. The test must prove no later event or
   Send occurs; it must report partial input honestly when an earlier event
   already ran.
2. **BLOCKER — the recipient source does not exist before every mutation in
   profile-originated message flows.** `plan:3086-3092,3112-3117` requires the
   thread-header recipient on every action, but `linkedin.message` first
   clicks the profile's Message control (`src/linkedin.zig:355-363`) and
   `instagram.dm` first clicks Message on the profile
   (`src/instagram.zig:171-175`); those clicks create/open the composer whose
   thread header contains `message_input`/`dm_input`. Specify staged identity:
   before opening the composer, bind the exact unique visible profile owner to
   the approved recipient; after it opens, bind the exact unique visible
   thread recipient before every text/edit/Send event. Conversation-URL
   LinkedIn can start at the second stage. Reds need a wrong profile owner
   before the opener click and a wrong thread owner after it. The blanket
   `__input == []` assertion must be stage-aware: the latter case may include
   the approved opener click but must contain no typing or Send. Apply the
   same exactly-one-visible/non-hidden rule to every DOM account marker, not
   only the recipient and Instagram nav link.
3. **BLOCKER — post-approval cancellation has no state/outcome contract.** The
   prompt rule at `plan:3095` says result, error, Stop and `session_ended`
   revoke an open card, including a running approved job. The state machine at
   `:3107-3110` permits `revoked/closed/crashed` only while consent is pending;
   after `approved`, it lists only run outcomes and tests only mismatch and
   timeout. Define what Stop, prompt end, session end, window close and crash
   do after approval but before the first mutation and between flow steps;
   specify cancellation of the queued/running engine job, whether the terminal
   row is `revoked`, `closed`, `crashed` or `unknown` after partial input, and
   force each ordering. Every card still needs exactly one `approvalend` and
   no dispatch after cancellation wins.
4. **BLOCKER — the plan's authoritative contracts still disagree.** D10 at
   `plan:518` omits story-view from “no dry run”; `:522,524-527` still binds
   cloneable `target_fp` and checks only a flow's committing step; S8.2 at
   `:3002` labels close/crash `expired`; S8.6 and T5 at `:3020-3025,1434`
   still specify `target_fp`; map F at `:1419` still has broker-side
   `revalidate`; and the files-touched list at `:3045` still assigns checks to
   `flow_steps`/`engine` rather than the action's `automation.js` task. Most
   importantly, the canonical D7b observation table at `:450-474` contains
   only `DRAWER approval`; it defines neither `approvalrect`, `approvalstate`
   nor `approvalend`, even though D7b is the plan's exact row schema. Rewrite
   these instead of relying on “S8 in detail wins,” and bind the table/count
   tests to the one canonical contract.

The docs diff passes `git diff --check`. No build, browser, display, live site
or credential was used. Findings and required reds were mailed to BlackRobin.

## MS6 Seatbelt profile-generator fix-forward (`463f288`)

Reviewed exact commit `463f288` on 2026-10-20 against macOS-plan MS6 and the
fixed network capability. **Verdict: BLOCKED (security-critical).** Moving the
writable path out of the Seatbelt source and into a named `-D` parameter closes
the original source-injection vector, the frozen valid-profile oracle is useful,
and the isolated unit suite passes 16/16. Three malformed capabilities still
survive the supposed fail-closed boundary:

1. **BLOCKER — the write grant can name the filesystem root.**
   `agent/host/zb_agent_host/sandbox_macos.py:138-143` accepts any string that
   starts with `/`. Both `dparams(scratchpad="/")` and
   `dparams(scratchpad="/tmp/..")` succeed. Once bound to
   `(subpath (param "SCRATCHPAD"))`, either can turn the one intended
   scratchpad write grant into a root write grant. The binding must require a
   canonical, non-root absolute scratchpad (preferably the expected LaunchSpec
   scratchpad), with root and dot-segment alias reds.
2. **BLOCKER — the profile kind is not type-checked.** `:64-105` accepts
   numeric `0` as `is_hook`, renders the CLI/helper profile, and includes the
   egress endpoint. Require an exact boolean and cover integer, null and string
   near-misses.
3. **BLOCKER — the network policy is not the exact capability.** `:29,58-94`
   accepts `localhost` for egress, only one bridge, or extra/wrong bridge
   ports. The authoritative mapping at macOS plan `:1581-1593` is literal
   `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` plus exactly `127.0.0.1:51091` and `:31337`, with a
   hook receiving exactly the latter two and no egress. Missing, extra, wrong
   and non-literal forms must all be refused.

Direct display-free probes reproduced all six survivors (`/`, `/tmp/..`,
numeric `is_hook`, localhost egress, one bridge and an extra bridge). Broad
`file-read*` and blanket `mach-lookup` remain explicitly unwired later-MS6
work, not additional findings on this incremental generator. The blockers and
required reds were mailed to JadeBeacon in Agent Mail 6939.

## MS5 both-Mac setup lifecycle harness (`531ef10`)

Reviewed exact test-only commit `531ef10` on 2026-10-20 against macOS-plan rev
14 item 5. **Verdict: BLOCKED-for-test-safety/integrity.** The harness is
honest that it is not armed: it returns 3 while MS6 or the staged runtime is
absent, and an armed run hard-fails until the check-to-register case exists.
It also scrubs display variables and uses noninteractive, strict-host-key SSH.
Two defects prevent running or accepting it:

1. **BLOCKER — the EXIT trap can signal process group zero.**
   `tests/mac/ms5_setup_e2e.sh:35` substitutes `0` when its PGID file does not
   exist. That is the ordinary state on both current NOT-ARMED exits. On macOS,
   `pkill -g 0` denotes the caller's own process group, so the cleanup can kill
   the remote test shell/group before deletion and can corrupt the claimed
   exit-3 result. Cleanup must signal only a present, numeric, greater-than-one
   PGID whose saved setup identity/group invariants have been checked; otherwise
   it must skip the signal. A local non-live test must exercise early exit and
   malformed/missing PGID data and prove group zero is never passed.
2. **BLOCKER-for-oracle — the setup child is selected ambiguously.** `:56`
   takes the first result of `pgrep -P "$B"`. The census could therefore follow
   a different direct child while the intended setup process escapes. Require
   exactly one matching setup child, verify its executable/argv, then require
   `PGID == PID` before saving or signalling that group. A decoy-child mutant
   must fail.

`bash -n tests/mac/ms5_setup_e2e.sh` passed. The remote harness was deliberately
not run because its cleanup is unsafe. Findings were mailed to BlueBeaver in
Agent Mail 6940.

## MS6 setup profile and generated-profile gate (`45bbbff`, `119089a`, `1c2ec20`)

Reviewed exact commits `45bbbff`, `119089a` and `1c2ec20` on 2026-10-20.
**Verdict: BLOCKED (`45bbbff`, `119089a`) and BLOCKED-for-tests (`1c2ec20`)
on one shared R1 execution-boundary defect.**

The CLI/helper generator improvements are sound in isolation. `119089a`
validates input as literal `127.0.0.1` but emits Seatbelt's required
`localhost:<port>` syntax; JadeBeacon's both-Mac run proved the production
generated CLI/hook profiles parse and keep the process-info canary contained.
The exact Linux unit suite at `45bbbff` passed 24/24. The later Darwin red also
correctly adopts the context-manager lifetime rather than treating the profile
as a permanent argv file.

The setup profile itself cannot satisfy its production contract:

- authoritative drawer-plan section 3c.7 (`plan:995-1008`) distinguishes
  `cli --version`, which needs no network, from the R1 route probe, which starts
  a one-shot server on the sandbox's `127.0.0.1:<port>` and runs the CLI
  against it;
- `sandbox_macos.py:158-183,209-232` uses one profile with no network grant for
  both operations; and
- `119089a` proves only that that setup profile parses and runs `/usr/bin/true`,
  while `1c2ec20` drives only `cli_version` and positively asserts the absence
  of a network rule.

Unlike Linux bwrap, Seatbelt does not give setup a private loopback namespace;
the R1 bind/connect is therefore denied and normal setup can never select the
only approved token route. Before `seatbelt_ready` changes, split the setup
capability by operation: version remains network-free; R1 pre-binds or chooses
one exact loopback port without a reuse race, permits only that endpoint, and
drives the real `probe_r1`/`route_probe` chain on both Macs while a separate
host-loopback decoy stays unreachable. Also harden the temporary profile open
with exclusive/no-follow 0600 creation, write-all and fsync; cover collision,
symlink and exception cleanup. Findings were mailed to JadeBeacon and
BlueBeaver in Agent Mail 6958.

## WS0.7 listener-churn red and green (`c4d4561`, `59e5fac`, `2af0d7a`)

Reviewed this exact chain on 2026-10-20. **Verdict: BLOCKED.** The test mechanics
are deterministic: the exact red produced its intended one failure and three
passes, and the exact `2af0d7a` hostless suite passed **98 tests with 17 live
skips**. `59e5fac` itself only deletes the unregistered red and has no
independent green value.

The proposed rule is not yet an approved contract and its implementation is
internally inconsistent:

- authoritative Windows-plan WS0.7 (`plan:767-775`) still requires the
  listener set to stay unchanged; the field-design document labels this an
  owner/RoseCat-approved future proposal (`design:58-79`);
- that proposal and `c4d4561:8-11` permit only post-only additions by a known
  PID and state that a dropped listener fails, but the red's alleged benign
  case replaces 49664 with 49700 and the green explicitly accepts arbitrary
  ephemeral drops; and
- PID alone is not stable ownership across the interval. A recycled PID
  inherits the exemption, while any pre-existing listener owner can add any
  number of high ports.

The Windows plan must first name one rule for additions, drops and replacements.
The schema then needs a stable owner identity obtainable by the standard-user
probe (at least PID plus process creation time, failing closed when it is not
available), with reds for reuse, drop-only, one-to-many, replacement and a
port swap between two pre-existing owners. Service ports remain invariant.
Findings were mailed to AzureRidge in Agent Mail 6960.

## Chat drawer S8 approval design, rev 16.20.40 (`61dc66d`)

Reviewed exact docs commit `61dc66d` on 2026-10-20. **Verdict: BLOCKED.** It
closes rev 16.20.39's recipient-stage and stale-authoritative-text findings:
the profile owner is checked before an opener, the thread header before text or
Send, all DOM account markers are exactly-one visible matches, and D7b plus
the outcome/state tables now agree. It also correctly recognizes that page
handlers execute synchronously inside `dispatchEvent`. Two boundary errors
remain:

1. Guarding before `editableInsert` is still check-then-act. Production
   `automation.js:977-980` dispatches `beforeinput`, then at `:982-998` performs
   `execCommand` or range insertion. An untrusted `beforeinput` handler can
   change the recipient/account/target between those points. Require a second
   guard after `beforeinput` returns and before insertion, plus a
   contenteditable red that changes the recipient and proves zero characters
   are inserted.
2. `engine.External.cancel` is native Zig state and cannot be read from inside
   one synchronous JavaScript evaluation. A Stop arriving during a long
   `dom.type` cannot affect the proposed per-event JS guard; the entire action
   can finish before control returns. Either split/chunk the action across
   event-loop/eval boundaries under the ticket and check native cancel between
   chunks, or explicitly make one action uninterruptible and specify that
   outcome. A real held-long-type test, not only a scripted engine, must prove
   any promised mid-action cancellation.

Findings were mailed to BlackRobin in Agent Mail 6964.

## MS6 macOS backend launch capability (`9c234e7`)

Reviewed security-sensitive commit `9c234e7` on 2026-10-20. **Verdict:
BLOCKED.** The backend's immutable `Network` values are correct: chat uses its
validated per-session loopback endpoint, `EGRESS_ALLOW`, and the two bridge
ports; login changes only the allowlist and removes the bridges. The exact
display-scrubbed unit suite passed 34/34. The launch artifact nevertheless
breaks the home and per-session contracts:

1. `sandbox_macos.py:332-334` writes `agent-cli.sb` under `home.runtime` on
   every launch. In the production layout, `runtime` is the fixed link to
   `current/runtime`, inside a published `dist-<n>` that must never be written
   after publish (drawer plan `:278-286,312`). The unit fixture substitutes a
   plain writable runtime directory and therefore bypasses this topology.
2. Every backend/session uses the same pathname. A two-backend reproduction at
   the exact commit created spec A for port 52346 and spec B for 52347. Both
   argv values named the same profile; after B, A's file contained 52347 and
   no 52346. Thus a held LaunchSpec can silently apply another session's proxy
   policy before `sandbox-exec` consumes it, contrary to the immutable spec and
   the per-session endpoint contract (macOS plan `:1581-1587`).
3. The shared `LaunchSpec.mounts` contract says it enumerates every exposed
   path (`sandbox.py:81-83`), but this spec reports only scratchpad while the
   applied profile still grants `file-read*` and ignores `ro_paths` and
   `state_dirs`. The module itself says the renderer must not be wired before
   read and mach-lookup curation. The semantic spec is therefore not yet a
   truthful description of the applied policy.

The fix needs a unique, securely created no-follow profile outside the
immutable published build, an artifact lifetime that lasts through spawn and
then cleans up, plus production-layout and two-live-spec reds. Symlink,
collision, partial-write and cleanup cases must fail closed. The semantic
filesystem contract must match the profile before platform dispatch, or this
increment must remain explicitly non-consumable. Findings and the exact
cross-session reproduction were mailed to JadeBeacon in Agent Mail 6972.

## Chat drawer S8 approval design, rev 16.20.41 (`ca1b5d6`)

Reviewed exact docs commit `ca1b5d6` on 2026-10-20. **Verdict: BLOCKED.** It
correctly closes the two conceptual boundaries from `61dc66d`: the expectation
guard now runs again after a synchronous page callback and before the next
page-visible write, and native cancellation is observed only between separate
JavaScript evaluations. Four implementation and test contracts are still
inconsistent or incomplete:

1. The keydown red contradicts the new guard rule. Plan `:3126` requires the
   guard after keydown and before the value write, but `:3130` still expects one
   character and `sent.chars = 1` after a keydown handler changes the recipient.
   It must expect zero characters, with the dispatched keydown counted as an
   event, or move the test's change to `input` if one character is intended.
2. The canceled-`beforeinput` red does not model a Draft.js-style editor. Such
   a handler may synchronously update its own model or DOM before returning.
   The new guard can prevent automation's later `execCommand` or range insert,
   but cannot undo that page-side edit. The plan must test this case and must
   not call it “nothing sent”: `sent.events` includes the dispatched event even
   when direct `sent.chars` is zero, and the outcome needs a conservative
   partial/unknown classification. A simpler handler that only changes the
   recipient may still prove no direct insert and no `input` event.
3. The chunk unit at `:3134,3140,3148` is only called “characters.” It must be a
   named Unicode-code-point limit, matching JavaScript `for...of`
   (`automation.js:942-955`) and `utf8CountCodepoints`
   (`flow_steps.zig:337-340`), with a multibyte/non-BMP boundary red.
4. `data.sent` is per JavaScript evaluation, but the plan does not say how the
   engine aggregates it over chunks. Require cumulative code-point and event
   counts from all completed chunks plus the failing chunk. A red should let
   chunk 1 succeed, change the recipient after three characters of chunk 2,
   and require 19/total, no later chunk and no Send; the boundary-cancel red
   remains 32/200.

The existing real hold before chunk 3 proves cancellation between evaluations,
not arrival during an evaluation. A bounded in-evaluation handler case is a
SHOULD if the “within one chunk” latency claim is retained. This docs-only
review ran no code gate. Findings were mailed to BlackRobin in Agent Mail 6976.

   `sandbox-exec` consumes it, then removes it on success, failure,
   cancellation or child exit. Only the tests install an external
   `rmtree` cleanup. A comment that the caller owns it is not an executable
   lifetime contract.
2. If `os.open` fails, the new directory remains; if the single `os.write`
   short-writes, or chmod/fstat fails, both a partial file and its directory
   remain. These paths fail closed but violate the required cleanup contract.
3. `test_sandbox_macos.py:339-405` uses a direct `runtime` directory rather
   than the real fixed link into immutable `current/dist-<n>`. Its collision
   assertion is a separate `os.open` after success, not a collision or symlink
   attack driven through `_materialize_profile`; short-write and cleanup cases
   are also absent.

The fix needs an owned lease/context at the spawn boundary and injected
open/write/chmod/fstat, collision, symlink, production-layout and cleanup reds.
The consumable flag must remain false until that and filesystem/mach curation
land. NIT: the `launch_spec` docstring still says it writes to `home.runtime`.

## R1 Darwin process-walk fix-forward (`4cec07b`)

Reviewed exact commit `4cec07b` on 2026-10-20. **Verdict: BLOCKED.** The
higher-level change is directionally correct: only `ProcessLookupError` is
skipped, other census/path errors propagate, and `_cli_env_clean` maps a walk
error to false. The focused suite passes 31/31. The native libproc oracle,
however, models the wrong ABI behavior.

Apple's libproc implementation converts an underlying `proc_listpids` failure
to return 0, after which `proc_listchildpids` also returns 0—not -1. Production
`children()` checks only negative results, while its new tests fake -1. A real
denied or vanished child census can therefore still become an apparently
successful empty list. Each native call must clear errno first, capture it
immediately afterward, and treat result 0 with nonzero errno as failure while
accepting result 0 with errno 0 as a real empty list. Reds must use the real
zero-plus-errno shape for both query and fill calls and include a stale-errno
control. Clearing errno around `proc_pidpath` is also needed to remove the same
ambiguity. Finding mailed to BlueBeaver in Agent Mail 7015.

## MS6.3 fd-3 reopen gate (`1cb5d2a`)

Reviewed exact test-only commit `1cb5d2a` on 2026-10-20. **Verdict:
BLOCKED-for-tests as the MS6.3 hard gate; useful lower-level Seatbelt probe.**
The new script is wired into both legs of `ms6_gate.sh`, generates the real CLI
profile, and has a meaningful denial control. Its helper reopens `/dev/fd/3`,
compares the exact synthetic canary, and the trailing deny rules show that the
positive depends on the profile's `file-read*` grant. Local clean-export
checks passed `/bin/sh -n` and compiled the C helper with
`-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`; the unsandboxed helper read its canary.

It does not yet prove the contract named by the plan. MS6.3 requires the
reopen to work **with the macOS CLI on both arches**
(`2026-10-14-14-30-macos-launch-tdd-plan.md:1608-1609`), but
`ms6_3_fd3_reopen_test.sh:29-31,61-63` executes only a C stand-in. It never
executes the pinned/bundled Claude CLI and never proves that CLI consumes the
announced `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE_DESCRIPTOR`. More importantly, the
test supplies fd 3 with shell input redirection from a regular file, whereas
the production R1 wrapper supplies fd 3 as one end of a Unix socketpair
(`agent/host/zb_agent_host/token.py:101-130`). A regular-file
`open("/dev/fd/3")` can pass while the production socket channel or the CLI's
actual read path fails. The current token contract even records that the CLI
reads a socket descriptor directly and only reopens a pipe/FIFO
(`token.py:3-8`), which conflicts with the test's assertion that the macOS CLI
reopens it.

Keep this probe, but do not call MS6.3 closed until a fix-forward resolves that
contract with evidence: use the production socketpair channel and the real

## macOS Seatbelt self-introspection exception (`aa83b5f`)

Reviewed exact security-critical commit `aa83b5f` on 2026-10-20. **Verdict:
APPROVED.** The production generator keeps the blanket
`(deny process-info*)` and adds only
`(allow process-info* (target self))` to the CLI/helper, hook, login and setup
profiles (`sandbox_macos.py:179-183,221-226`). This does **not** grant one
sandboxed process access to a sibling, parent, child or another process in the
same sandbox. `self` is the process performing the operation; a forked hook
therefore gets introspection of that hook itself, not of the token-bearing CLI.

This conclusion has three independent anchors:

- Chromium's real Seatbelt unit test uses deny-`process-info*` plus a
  self-scoped `process-info-pidinfo` allow, proves the query for `getpid()`
  succeeds, then proves the otherwise identical query for `getppid()` fails
  with `EPERM`: <https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/132.0.6834.70/sandbox/mac/seatbelt_unittest.cc#114>.
- WebKit's production WebProcess profile first denies `process-info*`, then
  restores its needed operations with `(target self)`, confirming that this is
  the platform's intended self-only filter shape:
  <https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebKit/WebProcess/com.apple.WebProcess.sb.in#L2504-L2514>.
- The repo's both-Mac generated-profile gate uses the exact emitted CLI and
  hook profiles against a live sacrificial sibling. The unsandboxed control
  must expose the canary, while both sandboxed probes must report `CONTAINED`
  (`ms6_generated_profile_test.sh:45-66`). JadeBeacon reports that this stayed
  green on Intel and arm64 after the exception, while Python changed from
  exit 132 under the bare deny to exit 0 under all three generated profiles.

The setup and ordinary generators are pinned byte-for-byte by their frozen
references, including both the blanket deny and exact self filter
(`test_sandbox_macos.py:202-209,225-296`). A clean-export Linux run of the
registered unit module passed **49/49** under `-X dev`; exact-SHA shell syntax
and Python compilation also passed. The Mac runtime-start addition is
discriminating: dropping the self exception makes the actual Python launch
exit 132 on both architectures. No full Linux gate was needed for this
three-file Mac-policy fix; the owner reports the complete `ms6_gate.sh` green
on both Mac architectures.

**SHOULD-for-tests:** `ms6_generated_profile_test.sh:78-81` tries to capture
the failed Python exit code after a command substitution, but `set -e` exits
at the assignment before `rc=$?` and the named `FAIL` row. The regression
still fails closed, so this does not weaken the oracle, but an `if out=$(...);`
shape should preserve the promised diagnostic. Also make the setup-profile
sibling probe direct when the pending R1 kernel gate is green; today the real
kernel sibling oracle directly covers generated CLI and hook profiles, while
the identical setup rule is pinned by the frozen oracle.

## Unified MS6 hard-gate harness red/green (`79f9933`, `3bd5727`)

Reviewed the exact pair on 2026-10-21. Independent clean exports reproduce the
reported transition: exact `79f9933` fails **6/6** because the driver and entry
are absent, while exact `3bd5727` passes **6/6** under display-scrubbed
`python3 -X dev`. The green registers the suite additively in both
`test-mac-census` and the Linux aggregate. The NOT ARMED entry exits 3 before
the current script contains any network operation, and the deliberately
failing MS6.6(B) placeholder prevents the future driver from certifying that
case. The single-harness topology matches approved rev 18.1.

**`79f9933` is BLOCKED-for-tests and `3bd5727` is BLOCKED.** Two load-bearing
harness properties are not safe or durably observed:

1. **BLOCKER — process groups are signalled twice.** `Harness.spawn_group`
   appends the process, then unconditionally calls `_reap` in its `finally`
   (`tests/mac/hard_gate/harness.py:36-47`). It never removes or marks that
   entry. `Harness.close` later walks the same list and calls `_reap` again
   (`:71-73`); `_reap` calls `os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL)` before checking the
   process state (`:49-56`). After the first `wait`, that numeric process-group
   id can be reused, so cleanup can kill an unrelated group. A deterministic
   fake-process check confirms two `killpg` calls. Make ownership consumption
   idempotent while retaining the required leader-exited/descendant-survives
   group kill.
2. **BLOCKER-for-tests — the lifecycle and pre-network claims bypass the
   suite.** None of the six tests calls `spawn_group`; normal completion,
   timeout, a leader that exits before a group child, pipe closure, repeated
   `close`, no survivors and exactly-once signalling are all untested even
   though this is the seam both security cases will consume. The NOT ARMED
   test (`ms6_hard_gate_driver_test.py:120-130`) checks only exit 3 and a text
   substring. It hardcodes the real `/usr/bin:/bin` PATH and overrides only the
   ARM host, so it neither observes “before any network” nor safely prevents a
   later guard-regression from reaching the default Intel host. Give it
   recording/refusing `ssh`/`scp`/network shims, set every host to a canary, and
   assert zero invocations for both missing-pins and pins-present-but-staging-
   absent states.

The ordinary driver rules—failed check, raise, no check, missing NAME/run,
duplicate NAME, empty case set and successful scratch cleanup—are otherwise
implemented fail closed. This review does not require the MS6.3 or MS6.6(B)
real cases before the MS5 pins decision; it requires the shared seam they will
inherit to be safe and mutation-protected first. No full gate was started
because BlackRobin held the shared slot.

### MS6 harness lifecycle and zero-network red (`554f36c`)

**APPROVED as the unregistered failing-first red.** An independent clean export
of exact `554f36c` reproduces the reported split: **3/7 fail** on the old seam.
The normal and leader-exited/child-survives cases observe SIGKILL only after the
leader has already been reaped, and calling `close()` twice produces two extra
signals. The timeout, 3 MiB output and two NOT ARMED cases already pass, so the
red is not a blanket missing-file failure.

The signal wrapper records both the group id and whether its leader still has
a `/proc/<pgid>` entry at the instant of the real `killpg`, then requires one
SIGKILL while that leader is unreaped. The outliving-child case additionally
censuses the actual child until it is gone. Together with the timeout, large
pipe output and repeated-close cases, this directly covers the lifecycle seam
that `79f9933` omitted.

Both gate cases run a copied entry in a throwaway git repository, prepend
recording/refusing shims for the planned remote/network tools, replace both
hosts and both keys with canaries, and require the call log to remain empty.
They independently cover missing pins and pins present with staging absent.
That is a durable discriminator for the current shell transport design and
closes the red-side portion of the zero-network finding.

**SHOULD-for-tests:** `alive()` performs `kill(pid, 0)` and then opens
`/proc/<pid>/stat` without catching disappearance between those operations
(`ms6_hard_gate_harness_test.py:53-61`). Treat `FileNotFoundError` as dead to
avoid a harmless child-exit race making the green flaky. This is noisy/fail-
closed, not a false-green blocker. The tests remain intentionally unregistered
until the production green lands; `3bd5727` stays blocked meanwhile.

### MS6 harness lifecycle green (`5ee7c1f`)

**APPROVED.** Exact `5ee7c1f` passes the registered harness lifecycle suite
**7/7** and the driver suite **5/5** in a clean, display-scrubbed export under
`python3 -X dev`. The new implementation waits for the leader with
`waitid(..., WNOWAIT)`, so the leader remains an unreaped zombie and protects
the process-group id; it then sends one group `SIGKILL`, reaps the leader, joins
both pipe readers and closes the pipes (`tests/mac/hard_gate/harness.py:43-77`).
Each owned entry is marked consumed before cleanup, so the driver's later
`close()` calls cannot signal the same numeric group again (`:61-73,90-92`).

The former weak NOT ARMED assertion was removed from the driver suite. The
registered replacement tests both missing-pins and pins-present/staging-absent
states with refusing, recording `ssh`, `scp`, `sftp`, `curl`, `nc` and `rsync`
shims and canary values for both hosts and keys; both require zero invocations
(`tests/e2e/ms6_hard_gate_harness_test.py:100-139`). The suite also observes
normal output, timeout, an outliving child, 3 MiB of output, the unreaped-leader
condition at the real signal and repeated `close()` (`:47-98`). The six reported
mutants independently remove exactly-once consumption, reorder reap before
kill, kill only the leader, remove the deadline, reach SSH before the guard, or
let pins alone arm the gate; each is killed by this suite.

This cumulatively closes the two blockers on `3bd5727`; the original
`79f9933`/`3bd5727` hard-gate harness chain is approved through `554f36c` and
`5ee7c1f`. The earlier `/proc` disappearance SHOULD is non-blocking and remains
advisory; it cannot false-green the cleanup invariant.

## macOS launch egress-port / Session red (`a0c568d`)

**APPROVED as the unregistered failing-first red.** The exact commit adds only
`agent/host/tests/test_launch.py`; neither `build.zig` nor production code is

## macOS grouped spawn with stdin/stdout (`214b9ad`, `06f0e35`)

**`214b9ad` is BLOCKED-for-tests; `06f0e35` is BLOCKED.** The red is genuinely
failing-first on both Mac architectures according to the owner's exact-SHA
evidence, and the green covers the important primary path: a new process-group
leader, stdin/stdout pipe round-trip, EOF shutdown, inherited `-1` streams,
Darwin `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT`, explicit inheritance of descriptors 0-2,
and refusal of stream descriptors in 0-2. The existing
`zb_agent_spawn_group` body is unchanged, and the production source compiles on
Linux with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`. Two correctness/coverage defects prevent
approval:

1. **BLOCKER — an equal source descriptor is closed before its second dup.**
   The public contract permits any descriptor above 2 for each stream, and the
   commit explicitly tries to support equality by suppressing the second
   `addclose`. But the actions are ordered `dup2(fd, 0)`, `close(fd)`, then
   `dup2(fd, 1)` (`src/agent_spawn_posix.c:48-53`). Compiling the exact seam and
   passing the same open descriptor for stdin and stdout returns `EBADF` (9),
   with no child. Enqueue both `dup2` actions before closing each unique source,
   or explicitly reject equality with `EINVAL` and narrow the header contract;
   add a discriminating case (a duplex socket is suitable if equality remains
   supported).
2. **BLOCKER-for-tests — the “exactly fds 0 1 2” census sees only 0-255.**
   `child_main` stops at 256 (`tests/mac/spawn_group_io_test.c:37-45`), so a
   leaked browser socket at a higher descriptor would pass the literal security
   oracle. Plant one inheritable descriptor at a known high number (for example
   with `F_DUPFD` at 300) and make the child census cover it. The current low
   planted descriptor does correctly kill the no-`CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` mutant, but
   it is not the whole exact-fd claim.

**SHOULD-for-tests:** `read_line(..., secs)` performs a blocking `read`, so its
10-second argument is not a deadline (`spawn_group_io_test.c:58-74`). Silence
can hold a leg until the outer 240-second SSH timeout. Poll/select or a
nonblocking descriptor would give a bounded local failure and useful output.

No aggregate gate was run: this slice is a manual two-Mac gate and the review
used the reported 9/9-per-architecture evidence, syntax/diff checks, a local
strict C compile and the equal-descriptor reproducer. Before macOS agent launch
is armed, the corrected Mac gate also needs a durable place in the applicable
hard-gate sequence rather than relying on a one-time manual invocation.

### macOS grouped-spawn fix-forward (`51780e3`, `1251c29`)

**APPROVED; these commits cumulatively close the blockers on `214b9ad` and
`06f0e35`.** The new red drives the public same-descriptor contract with one
end of a real Unix socketpair and reports the old implementation's `EBADF` on
both Mac architectures. The green queues both `dup2` actions before either
unique source is closed, so a single duplex descriptor can become both stdin
and stdout without a closed-source action (`src/agent_spawn_posix.c:48-53`).
The header states that behavior explicitly.

The exact-FD oracle now raises the soft descriptor limit when necessary,
plants a second inheritable descriptor at 300, scans beyond it, and requires
every child census to be exactly `0 1 2`. The reported no-
`POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` mutant exposes both fd 3 and fd 300 on x86_64 and
arm64. `read_line` polls before each read, making its local deadline real
rather than relying on the outer SSH timeout (`spawn_group_io_test.c:72-91,
96-106,117-132`).

Independent Linux validation compiled the production seam with
`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, passed one socket descriptor for both streams to
`/bin/cat`, observed a successful spawn and exact `roundtrip\n` echo, then
closed the write side and reaped status 0. Shell syntax and exact-diff checks
also passed. Darwin's exact-FD behavior is accepted from the reported
four-case gate on both Macs and its discriminating mutants. The manual test
still needs a durable place in the relevant macOS hard-gate chain before
launch is armed; that integration task is not a remaining defect in this C
seam.

## Windows build-driver hardening (`42c797b`)

**BLOCKED; `defb5a2`/`b32f285` remain open.** The checked command encoding is
correct: with `pipefail`, either encoder failure or an empty result stops before
the build SSH call, and the new injected `iconv` failure exercises that path.
Changing the remote preparation separators from a lone `&` to `&&` also fixes
the concrete masking bug. The focused hermetic suite passes **22/22**, and shell
syntax, Python compilation and exact-diff checks are clean.

The claimed atomic artifact/provenance publication is still not atomic.
`tests/windows/build-on-windows.sh:135-145` renames the new manifest over
`$out.sha`, then separately renames the new executable over `$out`. A crash or
second-rename failure between those operations leaves either an old executable
beside the new commit SHA, or a manifest without its executable. The first case
is especially dangerous because the later census can attribute the old binary
to the new source commit. `AtomicProvenance` only makes the manifest path
unwritable before either publish; it neither plants an old valid pair nor cuts
or fails the second rename, so this mismatch survives the new oracle.

Publish a complete version directory through one directory rename/current
swap, or establish and test an equivalent invariant in which interruption can
leave no executable with mismatched provenance. A red must start with an old
pair, fail/cut the second publication, and reject every surviving mismatched
pair. **SHOULD-for-tests:** the staging red only inspects the SSH command for a
lone `&`; force the preparation failure and prove that the build invocation is
never reached, as the original finding required. Findings were sent to
AzureRidge in Agent Mail 7159.

Consequently the linear boundary is unchanged: **`26fdfff` remains the pushed
through SHA and `7d85cd5` remains open pending the two watched WS0 runs.** If
those runs pass, the earliest blocked descendant is still **`defb5a2`**, not a
later WS1 slice.

## Zig netd spawn integration (`21a6f70`, `849f849`)

**`21a6f70` is BLOCKED-for-tests; `849f849` is BLOCKED.** The implemented
pipe topology, strict ready-port parser, bounded `poll`, malformed/empty/deadline
failure mapping and C grouped-spawn seam are directionally right. With an
extra `_GNU_SOURCE` compile definition, the five committed Linux cases pass.
Three defects prevent acceptance:

1. **BLOCKER — a valid ready line followed by immediate exit is accepted as a
   live netd.** The red's “stays up” case checks only `pid > 0`
   (`tests/agent_host_posix_spawn_test.zig:22-28`). Production returns a `Netd`
   immediately after parsing the port (`src/agent_host_posix.zig:146-148`) and
   never observes whether that process already exited; the existing
   `decide(..., netd_exited_early)` helper is not called. Add a stand-in that
   writes an exact ready line and exits, require `NetworkFailure`, and use a
   real liveness oracle for the positive.
2. **BLOCKER — normal stop does not allow the documented EOF cleanup.**
   `Netd.stop()` closes stdin and immediately calls `zb_agent_kill_group`
   (`agent_host_posix.zig:90-94`), whose implementation sends `SIGKILL` before
   waiting. The plan relies on stdin EOF so netd can unlink its sockets and
   remove its directory; immediate SIGKILL is explicitly the crash path. Wait
   a bounded interval for clean EOF exit and use group kill only as the
   backstop; prove both the clean marker/cleanup path and the hung-child path.
3. **BLOCKER — the registered Linux test target does not compile as written.**
   `build.zig` adds `agent_spawn_posix.c` with only `-std=c11`. Reproducing that
   exact compile fails because `killpg` is undeclared; adding `_GNU_SOURCE`
   makes the same five tests pass. Fix the feature-test macro/header contract
   and prove the registered target rather than a manually augmented command.

The failure-path tests also need an observable no-child/no-fd-leak assertion;
merely receiving `NetworkFailure` does not prove the stand-in was reaped. Under
the post-incident safety rule, every test that actually sends a signal must run
inside `unshare --user --map-root-user --pid --fork --mount-proc`, and a mocked
`Popen` must patch both `os.kill` and `os.killpg` to raise. Findings were sent
to JadeBeacon, with BlackRobin and BlueBeaver copied, in Agent Mail 7161.

**`5e48fab` is BLOCKED-for-tests; `b3fda89` is BLOCKED cumulatively, although

## WS0 WTS lock-state mechanism (`5bef873`)

**BLOCKED for WS0 closure. SUPERSEDED LAYOUT FINDING:** the byte-offset
approval below was withdrawn on 2026-10-21 after a read-only dump of the real
232-byte `WTSINFOEXW` buffer. The replacement signal is the right one, but the
implementation reads the wrong field in addition to the failure-semantics and
watched-acceptance problems recorded here.

The following layout conclusion was **incorrect and is withdrawn**. Microsoft's
[`WTSINFOEXW`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wtsapi32/ns-wtsapi32-wtsinfoexw)
wraps a four-byte `Level` before the union, and
[`WTSINFOEX_LEVEL1_W`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wtsapi32/ns-wtsapi32-wtsinfoex_level1_w)
places `SessionId`, `SessionState` and `SessionFlags` next, but the union is
eight-byte aligned: `Data` starts at byte 8, `SessionId` is at byte 8,
`SessionState` at byte 12, and `SessionFlags` at byte 16. Reading byte 12
therefore reads the active session's state (`WTSActive == 0`), not its lock
flag, and falsely reports both locked and unlocked sessions as locked. Demoting
`OpenInputDesktop` to a diagnostic matches the user's observed locked console,
where it incorrectly returned `Default`.

**BLOCKER — fail-open unknown state:**
`tests/windows/session_probe.ps1:44-51` returns `false` when the WTS query
fails or the flag is unknown and LogonUI is absent. That makes
`interactive_session=true`. `host_probe.ps1` then propagates only the derived
`locked`/`interactive_session`, and `gate.sh:235-238` accepts that result. An
unavailable or unknown authoritative signal must instead remain unknown or be
treated as locked, so the normal gate refuses it. The current fixture at
`tests/windows/host_live_test.py:483` explicitly pins the unsafe
`FB_OFF=False` result; replace it with a fail-closed oracle and mutation.

**BLOCKER-for-tests — the watched lock run can bypass WTS:**
`tests/windows/host_live_test.py:443-450` accepts a LogonUI observation instead
of a successful WTS query. The owner-watched locked case can therefore pass if
the P/Invoke, layout or actual SessionFlags read is broken. WS0 acceptance must
require `wts_lock_ok is True` and `session_flags == 0` on the genuinely locked
console. After it is unlocked, the normal watched run must likewise prove that
the real query returned `wts_lock_ok=true` and `session_flags=1`; the LogonUI
fallback can be tested independently but cannot substitute for the primary
mechanism.

**BLOCKER — the authoritative contract is stale:** the Windows plan still
binds the verdict to `OpenInputDesktop` and explicitly excludes WTS/LogonUI at
lines 11, 510-514, 713-715 and 725-726. It needs a fix-forward revision that
names WTSINFOEX, the fail-closed unknown state, diagnostic-only input desktop,
and both exact watched observations. The old mechanism is also still described
in `tests/windows/host_probe.ps1:172-178` and `tests/windows/gate.sh:156-159`.

Independent exact-commit, display-free evidence:

```text

```

The throwaway export was deleted immediately. No VM or live desktop was
touched. After the blockers are fixed, the exact updated probe must be
restaged because its verified SHA changes; then the watched locked run with
`ZB_EXPECT_LOCKED=1` and the unlocked two-host `gate.sh --probe-only` run must

{"code":-32015,

violates plan `:3130-3131`, where chars count only a write or insert that

   boundary. Use a narrowly e2e-gated seam if WebKit cannot select that branch
   deterministically.
3. Preserve the existing successful-native-insert row proving that an actual
   inserted character still reports chars=1.

Moving `wrote` alone is insufficient: the fix must distinguish successful
native insertion, cancelled native input and a guarded fallback insertion.

## MS6.5 libproc sweep and both-Mac gate (`7fa8906`, `5c20710`)

**BLOCKED.** The pure classification helper remains sound and its exact-commit,
display-scrubbed clean-export check is green (4/4 steps, 5/5 tests), but the
production sweep and its destructive Mac test are not safe or complete enough
to accept. The 8/8 reports recorded by `5c20710` are execution evidence, not a
valid acceptance result, because the test can pass while the sweep examines
only part of the process table.

1. **BLOCKER — `proc_listallpids` is divided twice.**
   `src/agent_run_reaper.c:100-101` calls `proc_listallpids` and then divides
   the result by `sizeof(pid_t)`. Apple's implementation already converts the
   underlying byte count to a PID-entry count before returning. The loop
   consequently scans only about one quarter of the returned PID entries.
   Use the returned count directly, retry within a bound when capacity was
   filled, and mutation-test both the extra division and the sizing/fill race.
   Source: <https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/libsyscall/wrappers/libproc/libproc.c>.
2. **BLOCKER — deletion authority is not bound to a safe run marker.**
   `agent_run_reaper.c:87-93` accepts broad markers such as `/tmp` or a user's
   home and falls back to the unverified caller string when `realpath` fails.
   Require the canonical, app-owned, unique per-run directory pinned at
   creation, reject broad ancestors, and fail closed if it cannot be
   revalidated. A deleted or aliased marker cannot silently fall back.
3. **BLOCKER — identity and signal outcomes are not proved.** The UID read is
   before a potentially long marker scan, not immediately before SIGKILL; no
   process birth identity is pinned. Line 118 also ignores `kill`'s return.
   Pin and revalidate stable identity plus UID immediately before signalling;
   treat ESRCH as vanished and surface every other error.
4. **BLOCKER — the Mac gate can send unsafe signals.**
   `tests/mac/ms6_5_reaper_test.c:53` can call `kill(-1, 0)` after a failed
   spawn/read. Cleanup lines 82-83 raw-signal detached numeric PIDs, including
   an escaper already killed by the sweep and therefore eligible for PID
   reuse. `setsid()` is unchecked, exact census/sweep sets are not asserted,
   and timeout can strand 120-second children. Validate every PID before any
   kill/kill0, use held identity/control channels for cleanup, prove PGID
   escape, assert exact sets, and clean every exit path. Do not rerun this gate
   before that fix.
5. **BLOCKER — retiring the orphan gate drops still-binding coverage.** The
   deleted gate drove the production spawn/parent-watch lifecycle and a real
   setsid escape. The accept-with-cleanup decision withdraws the impossible
   no-survivors assertion, not the requirement that app stop/next start clean
   a real escaped descendant. Replace that production lifecycle coverage.
6. **BLOCKER — bounded result arrays silently truncate.** More than 512
   matches are reported as ordinary success. Return explicit overflow and
   never let a truncated survivor set authorize a “clean” result.

**SHOULD:** exercise cwd, executable, and open-FD positives through real

   (`engine.zig:642-669`), which is correct for a command's initial attempt but
   not for every new call made by `typeInChunks`. Check the shared deadline
   before every chunk after the first and return -32009 before eval, with the
   exact prior count. A fake-clock red must advance to/past the deadline after
   chunk one and observe exactly one evaluation.
3. **BLOCKER — ambiguous failures acquire falsely exact `data.sent`.**
   `withPriorSent` adds prior counts to every failure
   (`engine.zig:1796-1820`). If a later PagePort call times out or fails after
   the page may have processed some/all of its chunk, the reply claims only
   the prior chunks in the exact `sent` field. S8 distinguishes `partial` from
   `unknown` using this evidence. Add prior counts only when current dispatch
   is proved zero, or combine them with the guard's own exact counts. An
   ambiguous port/eval failure must remain unknown and cannot put a lower bound
   in the exact field. Red: chunk one succeeds; chunk two accepts the call and
   times out; its response cannot claim that only chunk one was sent.
4. **BLOCKER — `delay_ms: 0` contradicts the public contract.** The docs and
   commit say a guard cannot be combined with `delay_ms`, but router line 324
   rejects only positive values and the test explicitly accepts zero. Reject
   presence, as the humanize contract does; test absent accepted and both zero
   and positive values refused.

**SHOULD:** every successful chunk increments `run.attempts`, so a three-chunk
success with no retry reports `retry_count = 2`. Track retries separately from
scheduled chunks and pin root telemetry. Verdict sent to BlackRobin in Agent
Mail 7240.

## Canonical Darwin setup scratch (`3120af5`, `16bad65`)

**`3120af5` APPROVED as a causal red; `16bad65` APPROVED.** The red extends
the already-registered `test_setup_darwin_tmpdir` module, so the intermediate
commit intentionally makes the registered setup gate red; the green lands
immediately after it. Future reds for registered modules should remain in a
new unregistered file until their green, as BlueBeaver noted in Agent Mail
7403.

The production change does not widen the writable set. `tempfile.mkdtemp`
first creates a unique leaf directory (0700 by the Python contract), and
`os.path.realpath` then resolves only aliases in that already-created path;
the unique leaf remains the boundary. Both Darwin setup callers pass that
canonical leaf to `sandbox_macos.setup_sandbox`, whose `dparams` rejects a
non-absolute, non-canonical or root path and whose profile grants
`file-write*` only to `(subpath (param "SCRATCHPAD"))` plus the fixed character
devices. `HOME`, `TMPDIR` and the `SCRATCHPAD` binding all receive the same
canonical leaf. The two production callers either supply no extra environment
or only `PYTHONPATH`/`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, so they cannot replace `HOME`;
Darwin overwrites `TMPDIR` after merging the caller environment. Linux still
binds and changes directory to that one leaf. Cleanup targets the same
canonical leaf.

The red's symlinked-temp fixture accurately models `/tmp -> /private/tmp` and
requires the seam path to be under the real parent, equal to its own realpath,
and equal to both environment paths. In an exact `3120af5` archive, the
registered `test-agent-setup-ms5` step failed only that row, showing the old
`.../tmp/zb-setup-run-*` alias. In an exact `16bad65` archive inside a private
user/PID namespace:

- `zig build agent-host-win-import --summary all`: **3/3 steps**; and
- `zig build test-agent-setup-ms5 --summary all`: **22/22 steps, 14/14
  tests**, with `test_setup_darwin_tmpdir` **4/4**.

The throwaway trees were deleted immediately. The already-recorded defense in
depth SHOULD remains: `sandbox_macos.dparams` could itself require
`scratchpad == realpath(scratchpad)`, so any future caller that hands it an
alias refuses rather than receiving an ineffective grant. That is not a
blocker for these two current callers, which canonicalize the newly-created
leaf before the seam.
